name: account-reconciliation-standard
title: Account Reconciliation Standard
summary: Set a standard for balance-sheet reconciliations: purpose, frequency, evidence, and aging of open items.
example: Several balance-sheet accounts have no named preparer, and cash recs live in one person's inbox.
example_out: A standard that assigns owners, defines a proper recon, and moves evidence to a shared location without shared passwords.

name: accounts-payable-control
title: Accounts Payable Control
summary: Tighten payables so the company pays the right vendor, once, with evidence.
example: Two similar invoices from the same supplier were paid last quarter.
example_out: A control review that separates vendor setup from payment release and proposes a duplicate review list without accusing the supplier.

name: accounts-receivable-control
title: Accounts Receivable Control
summary: Review receivables so the aging means something and cash collection is a process, not a hope.
example: The AR aging shows a large over-90 bucket, and cash sits unapplied in the same report.
example_out: A review that reconciles the aging, separates disputes from overdue, and lists unapplied cash before anyone writes a chase note.

name: accrual-policy
title: Accrual Policy
summary: Draft a short accrual policy so estimates are consistent, documented, and reversed on purpose.
example: Bonus accruals are booked differently by two entities, and neither documents the driver.
example_out: A short draft policy covering their actual accruals, evidence, reversal, and an approver, marked as a draft.

name: audit-prep-pbc
title: Audit PBC Preparation
summary: Build a provided-by-client list that answers the auditor's request without dumping the entire file room.
example: The external auditor asked for revenue samples and the team is about to export every invoice with no index.
example_out: An indexed PBC with owners, report parameters, tie-out notes, and no shared passwords.

name: bank-reconciliation
title: Bank Reconciliation
summary: Reconcile book to bank and leave a list of items a human must clear, with no plugs.
example: The operating account reconciliation has an unexplained difference and three deposits in transit older than a month.
example_out: A reconciliation that shows the unexplained amount, classifies the old deposits as needing a decision, and does not plug the difference.

name: chart-of-accounts-design
title: Chart of Accounts Design
summary: Design a chart of accounts people can code to, with enough detail to manage and not so much that nobody agrees.
example: A growing firm has 400 accounts and still cannot see gross margin by service line.
example_out: A proposal that uses a dimension for service line, defines the accounts that change, and maps old balances forward.

name: expense-policy
title: Expense Policy Draft
summary: Draft a usable expense policy: what is allowed, who approves, and what evidence is required.
example: Managers are approving their own travel after the fact, and finance wants a one-page policy.
example_out: A draft with limits, evidence, a ban on self-approval above a threshold, and a logged exception path. Tax treatment is left to their advisor.

name: fixed-asset-register
title: Fixed Asset Register
summary: Review a fixed-asset register so additions, disposals, and depreciation have an owner and a trail.
example: The register net book value does not match the GL, and several laptops are still depreciating after people left.
example_out: A review that leads with the tie-out break, lists disposal questions, and proposes sample checks rather than silent write-offs.

name: intercompany-reconcile
title: Intercompany Reconciliation
summary: Reconcile balances and transactions between entities so the group is not adding numbers that do not eliminate.
example: Two subsidiaries disagree by a material amount on a management fee, and the group close is tomorrow.
example_out: A both-sides match, a classification of the difference, and a draft elimination that does not force a missing counterparty into existence.

name: internal-controls-walkthrough
title: Internal Controls Walkthrough
summary: Walk through one process and describe the control as it is actually performed, including where it can fail.
example: The team says vendor payments are 'reviewed' but cannot show what the reviewer looks at.
example_out: A walkthrough that states the risk, describes the review as undocumented, and recommends one evidence fix without claiming certification.

name: inventory-accounting
title: Inventory Accounting Review
summary: Review inventory accounting issues: cut-off, obsolescence, and the tie between the count and the ledger.
example: A year-end count is short of the GL, and the warehouse says some goods were shipped but still in the system.
example_out: A tie-out that isolates the shipped-not-relieved population and asks for cut-off evidence before anyone books a shrinkage number.

name: journal-entry-review
title: Journal Entry Review
summary: Review manual journals for purpose, support, and unusual patterns without accusing anyone on a hunch.
example: Several round-dollar journals hit revenue on the last day of the quarter.
example_out: A review list that flags those entries for support and purpose, without alleging misconduct.

name: management-accounting-pack
title: Management Accounting Pack
summary: Turn the ledger into a decision view: margins, cost centers, and a reconciliation back to the books.
example: Leaders want margin by service line, but half of delivery cost sits in a general pool.
example_out: A pack that shows contribution before allocation, labels the pool as unallocated, and bridges to the ledger.

name: month-end-close
title: Month-End Close
summary: Run a practical month-end close that produces one set of numbers and a short list of judgments.
example: The controller wants a soft close by day six and cash is still unreconciled on day five.
example_out: A close status that refuses sign-off on unreconciled cash, lists open judgments, and separates any late entries.

name: payroll-accounting-review
title: Payroll Accounting Review
summary: Review the payroll journal path from the payroll register to the ledger, including accruals and remittances.
example: The payroll register and the wage expense account have not matched for two months.
example_out: A tie-out of gross-to-journal, a mapping question on liabilities, and a control note on who reviews the register.

name: tax-calendar
title: Tax Calendar
summary: Build an internal calendar of tax and filing dates the user already knows they must meet, with owners. Not tax advice.
example: A company added a second state and the controller wants a calendar, but is unsure which filings apply.
example_out: A calendar of known filings, unconfirmed items marked as such, internal lead times, and a clear handoff to their tax advisor for the new state.

name: farm-cash-week
title: Farm Cash Week
summary: Review a farm's coming weeks of cash against known receipts and bills.
example: A note treats an unsigned grain contract as cash already coming.
example_out: A weekly view that labels the contract hoped and shows the break week without it.

name: farm-record-review
title: Farm Record Review
summary: Review farm records for completeness before a buyer, auditor, or lender asks.
example: A buyer asks for treatment records and the draft invents dates to look complete.
example_out: A review that lists the gap and refuses the invented dates.

name: food-safety-pack
title: Food Safety Pack
summary: Assemble a food-safety document pack from the practices they already run, for their auditor or buyer.
example: A pack includes a handwashing SOP the farm does not use, to satisfy a checklist.
example_out: A pack that marks the SOP as not in place and assigns an owner if they choose to adopt it.

name: season-plan
title: Season Plan
summary: Plan a season from fields, labor, and cash the farm can actually commit.
example: A plan adds a crop the only operator cannot harvest in the same week as the existing one.
example_out: A plan that shows the labor clash and asks which enterprise to cut.

name: agent-task-card
title: Agent Task Card
summary: Bound an agent task: the inputs, the tools, the stop rules, and the human owner.
example: An agent spec lets the bot email the customer and issue a credit.
example_out: A card that allows a draft and requires a person to send or credit.

name: ai-cost-note
title: AI Cost Note
summary: Estimate the cost of a proposed AI workflow from the user's prices and volumes.
example: A pitch says the bot will save $40,000 a month. No volume or price is attached.
example_out: A note that leaves the savings blank and prices only the calls they can count.

name: ai-data-note
title: AI Data Note
summary: Say what may be pasted into a model and what must stay in the source system.
example: Agents want to paste full tickets, including card last-fours and a home address.
example_out: A note that allows the complaint text and strips the card and address.

name: ai-eval-plan
title: AI Eval Plan
summary: Plan an evaluation from examples the user already has, with a pass rule they can apply.
triggers: how will we know it works
example: A team wants to claim 95 percent accuracy before any example is labeled.
example_out: A plan that refuses the 95 percent and names the examples still to label.

name: ai-incident-note
title: AI Incident Note
summary: Write up a bad model output the user observed, with the prompt, the harm, and the hold.
example: A draft refund of $20 was sent. The agent had not approved it. One case.
example_out: A note that records the sent draft, pauses auto-send, and does not call it a pattern yet.

name: ai-output-check
title: AI Output Check
summary: Check a model draft against the source text the user supplied.
example: A reply says the order shipped on 12 September. The ticket does not mention shipping.
example_out: A check that cuts the ship date and leaves the reply unsent.

name: ai-review-gate
title: AI Review Gate
summary: Place a human review where a model output can move money, a customer message, or a record.
example: Refund drafts are set to send at night with no reviewer on shift.
example_out: A gate that holds night drafts until the morning reviewer.

name: ai-use-case
title: AI Use Case
summary: Decide whether a task should use a model, who owns the failure, and what stays manual.
example: Support wants a bot to issue refunds with no review.
example_out: A note that keeps refunds with a person and limits the model to a draft.

name: ai-vendor-note
title: AI Vendor Note
summary: Compare AI vendors on data use, exit, and support the user can point to in a document.
example: A one-pager says the vendor is SOC 2 because the website has a badge.
example_out: A note that treats the badge as unverified until the report is in the file.

name: rag-source-note
title: RAG Source Note
summary: Decide which documents may sit in a retrieval set and which are stale or out of bounds.
example: A refund policy from 2023 is in the set next to the 2026 version.
example_out: A note that removes the 2023 file and names the 2026 file as the only refund source.

name: baggage-irregularity
title: Baggage Irregularity
summary: Record a bag irregularity with the tag, the flight, and the status they know.
example: Tag 8812 is delayed off KA412. A text told the passenger it would be at the house by 8 p.m.
example_out: A file that says delayed, and a correction that 8 p.m. was not known.

name: crew-duty-limit
title: Crew Duty Check
summary: Check a duty figure against the limit the user provides. Do not advise exceeding it.
example: The pairing is 14 hours. The limit they stated is 13. A note asks how to make it legal.
example_out: A check that says stop, with no workaround.

name: delay-message
title: Delay Message
summary: Write the passenger message from the delay facts the station can say.
example: KA412 has no new departure. A draft says 18:40 and a free hotel.
example_out: A message that says the new time is unknown and drops the hotel.

name: disruption-message
title: Disruption Message
summary: Write the customer message for a cancellation with the rebooking fact they have.
example: KA188 is cancelled. No seat is confirmed. A draft promises the 10:00 and a full refund.
example_out: A message that says cancelled, no seat yet, and no refund figure.

name: irrops-brief
title: Irregular Ops Brief
summary: Brief the station on a disrupted flight using the facts the controller has.
example: KA412 is late. The only fact is a ground hold. A draft blames maintenance.
example_out: A brief that says ground hold and drops the maintenance line.

name: route-result-note
title: Route Result
summary: Report a route day from the flights and the loads the user exported.
example: Four flights, one cancel, loads 80, 91, and 70 on the three that flew. Target load 85.
example_out: A day note that keeps the cancel and does not average it away.

name: station-open-check
title: Station Open Check
summary: Check the station open items against the list the station uses.
example: Fuel paperwork is open. The first wave is KA188 at 06:10. A draft says open the station anyway.
example_out: A check that holds KA188 until the fuel item is signed.

name: station-turn-note
title: Station Turn Note
summary: Record a turn delay with the minute it started and the cause the ramp lead wrote.
example: The turn was 55 minutes against 40. The ramp note says a late bag cart. A draft says cabin cleaning.
example_out: A note that keeps the bag cart and the 15 minutes.

name: dealer-launch-check
title: Dealer Launch Check
summary: Check whether a local launch day has the cars, the staff, and the offer the dealer can honor.
example: The ad says six test-drive cars. Two are on the ground. The payment in the ad was not calculated.
example_out: A check that cuts the ad to two cars and removes the payment.

name: dealer-morning-review
title: Dealer Morning Review
summary: Set the service morning from the appointments and the parts the dealer can see.
example: 14 appointments, 2 techs in, brake parts for RO 4418 are not in.
example_out: A board that holds 4418 and does not promise it today.

name: fleet-replace-note
title: Fleet Replacement Note
summary: Compare fleet units the user listed on age, cost, and downtime, without a forced replacement.
example: They can replace two vans. Three are old. One is on a safety hold for brakes.
example_out: A note that puts the safety-hold van first and leaves the third unfunded.

name: handover-checklist-auto
title: Vehicle Handover
summary: Check a handover against the items the dealer says the customer must see.
example: The car is due at 3 p.m. The recall check was not run. The draft marks it clear.
example_out: A checklist that blocks the keys until the recall check is actually run.

name: parts-backorder-note
title: Parts Backorder
summary: Tell the advisor what to say when a part is not in and a promise date is already on the RO.
example: RO 4418 brakes were promised today. The pads are backordered with no ETA.
example_out: A sentence that pulls today's promise and does not invent a date.

name: recall-owner-note
title: Recall Owner Note
summary: Draft the customer note for a recall using the notice the dealer has, not a homemade defect claim.
example: Notice 26-118 says park the vehicle. A draft tells the owner they can drive until the part arrives.
example_out: A note that repeats the park instruction and the booking path.

name: service-lane-plan
title: Service Lane Plan
summary: Plan the lane so promised times match the techs and the parts on hand.
example: Promised hours are 22. Two techs have 16 hours. Three jobs have no parts.
example_out: A plan that cuts the board to 16 hours and parks the parts-missing jobs.

name: warranty-file-review
title: Warranty File Review
summary: Check a warranty file for the documents their checklist requires before it is submitted.
example: The file has no photo of the failed pad and the cause line is blank.
example_out: A review that holds the claim until the photo and the tech's cause are in.

name: account-opening-ops
title: Account Opening Operations
summary: Review an account-opening checklist for identity steps they require, without collecting secrets into the chat.
example: Staff want to skip an identity step because the customer is in a hurry.
example_out: A checklist that keeps the step and routes any exception to the compliance owner.

name: credit-file-checklist
title: Credit File Checklist
summary: Checklist a credit file for missing information before a human credit officer decides.
example: A file is missing current financials and the draft says the borrower is strong.
example_out: A checklist that leaves the file incomplete and removes the strength claim.

name: liquidity-ladder
title: Liquidity Ladder
summary: Build a simple liquidity ladder from cash, committed inflows, and committed outflows.
example: A ladder treats an undrawn line as money already in the account.
example_out: A ladder that separates the line from cash and flags the first short bucket.

name: payment-run-review
title: Payment Run Review
summary: Review a payment run for duplicates, approvals, and changes to payee details.
example: A payment run includes a new account number received by email this morning.
example_out: A review that holds that item until the verified channel confirms it.

name: blog-assignment
title: Blog Assignment
summary: Assign a post with the reader, the question, the source, and the date.
example: An editor wants a post on Calgary grocery prices by Friday. The writer has four receipts and no other source.
example_out: An assignment limited to those receipts, or no Friday date.

name: blog-distribution
title: Blog Distribution
summary: Say where a finished post goes, based on channels the writer actually has.
example: A plan says email the list, post the full text in a Facebook group they do not run, and tag a grocer who has not agreed.
example_out: A note that keeps the email and cuts the group paste and the unagreed tag.

name: blog-edit
title: Blog Edit
summary: Edit a draft against the notes, and mark claims that the notes do not support.
example: A draft says groceries are up 18 percent. The notes have four receipts and no index.
example_out: An edit that cuts the 18 percent and leaves the receipt totals.

name: blog-outline
title: Blog Outline
summary: Outline a post from the assignment and the notes, with headings the writer can draft from.
example: The grocery post has notes for three receipts and a blank heading called 'the provincial trend'.
example_out: An outline that drops the trend heading until a source exists.

name: blog-refresh
title: Blog Refresh
summary: Update an old post with what changed, and label the update.
example: A 2024 post still says a permit costs $50. The writer has a 2026 fee sheet at $75.
example_out: An update line and a $75 figure tied to the fee sheet, with the 2024 date kept.

name: blog-series
title: Blog Series
summary: Plan a series where each post can stand alone and the writer has notes for each part.
example: A four-part small-business series has notes for pricing and hiring only.
example_out: A two-part plan, with the other parts unscheduled.

name: blog-source-note
title: Blog Source Note
summary: List what the post may cite, and what has to come out.
example: The draft cites a StatCan table the writer has not opened, plus four receipts they do have.
example_out: A note that allows the receipts and pulls the StatCan sentence.

name: blog-title-pack
title: Blog Title Pack
summary: Write title options that the draft can support, with no borrowed viral headline.
example: They want 'Grocery prices up 18 percent in Calgary' and the draft only has four receipts.
example_out: Three titles about those receipts, and a no on the 18 percent title.

name: change-order
title: Change Order Brief
summary: Brief a change order with the cause, the cost basis they have, and the time effect.
example: A superintendent wants a change order with a round number and no backup.
example_out: A brief that blocks the round number until backup exists and records the direction to proceed.

name: estimate-assumption-log
title: Estimate Assumption Log
summary: Log estimate assumptions so a bid can be explained without invented quantities.
example: An estimate assumes night work is included but the invitation excludes it.
example_out: A log that records the conflict and refuses to hide the exclusion.

name: punch-list
title: Punch List
summary: Turn a punch list into items with a location, an owner, and a done standard.
example: A punch list says 'finish lobby' with no owner.
example_out: A list of located items, with life-safety called out and an owner on each line.

name: rfi-writer
title: RFI Writer
summary: Write a request for information that states the conflict, the location, and the date the answer is needed.
example: An RFI asks the designer to 'see the attached and advise' with no question.
example_out: An RFI with one located question, a need-by date, and no invented detail.

name: safety-toolbox-talk
title: Safety Toolbox Talk
summary: Draft a toolbox talk for a specific site hazard, with the control the crew must use.
example: A draft says to skip the harness because the task is short.
example_out: A talk that requires the harness and stops the task if it is missing.

name: schedule-look-ahead
title: Schedule Look-Ahead
summary: Build a short look-ahead from constraints, not from a hopeful bar chart.
example: A look-ahead schedules a pour before the inspection the city requires.
example_out: A look-ahead that parks the pour behind the inspection and names the constraint owner.

name: site-daily-report
title: Site Daily Report
summary: Write a site daily report from observed work, weather, and safety notes, with no invented quantities.
example: A draft says the slab was poured though the crew was rained out.
example_out: A report that records the rain delay and leaves the pour unclaimed.

name: engagement-framing
title: Engagement Framing
summary: Frame a consulting engagement with the decision, the evidence, and what is out of scope.
example: A proposal promises a 20 percent savings number before any baseline exists.
example_out: A brief that replaces the number with a baseline task and a decision.

name: findings-readout
title: Findings Readout
summary: Read out findings with evidence, implications, and a recommendation the sponsor can reject.
example: A readout drops a critical finding because the sponsor disliked it in the dry run.
example_out: A readout that keeps the finding, labels it clearly, and offers the sponsor a decision.

name: interview-synthesis-client
title: Client Interview Synthesis
summary: Synthesize client interviews into themes with quotes the interviewee actually gave.
example: A synthesis says the CFO demanded a cut, and the note was anonymous and less specific.
example_out: A synthesis that keeps the anonymity rule and narrows the claim to the words in the note.

name: workshop-decision-record
title: Workshop Decision Record
summary: Turn a client workshop into a decision record rather than a photo of sticky notes.
example: Notes say the client chose a market, but the room only brainstormed.
example_out: A record that labels the market as an idea, not a decision, and lists the open choice.

name: audience-trust-note
title: Audience Trust Note
summary: Review a creator's recent posts for trust gaps: undisclosed deals, recycled claims, and metrics they cannot show.
example: Three gift posts in a month have no disclosure, and the creator wants a caption about authenticity.
example_out: A note that blocks the authenticity caption until those three posts are corrected.

name: brand-deal-brief
title: Brand Deal Brief
summary: Brief a brand deal so the creative, the disclosure, and the usage are agreed before anyone films.
example: A skincare brand wants 'cleared my acne in three days' and no mention that the post is paid.
example_out: A brief that replaces the cure claim with an honest test plan and requires a clear paid label.

name: content-batch-plan
title: Content Batch Plan
summary: Plan a batch filming day so the creator leaves with usable pieces, not a camera roll of half ideas.
example: A batch day list says 'film 20 ideas' and none of the ideas are written.
example_out: A plan for a smaller set of written cards, grouped by setup, with a file-naming rule.

name: content-creator-week
title: Creator Operating Week
summary: Plan a creator's week from the slots they can actually film, edit, and reply.
example: A plan has seven original videos and the creator has one evening free.
example_out: A week with one filmed piece, two cuts from it if time remains, and replies scheduled before new ideas.

name: content-repurpose-map
title: Content Repurpose Map
summary: Map one original piece into smaller posts without stripping the context or hiding the source.
example: A creator wants to clip a news clip they do not own and post it as their own faceless channel.
example_out: A refusal of that clip and a map that only cuts a video the creator filmed.

name: creator-boundary-note
title: Creator Boundary Note
summary: Write the boundaries a creator will keep: topics, deals, comments, and personal life.
example: A creator wants a boundary note that also includes a plan to dogpile a rival's comments.
example_out: A boundary note that declines hidden ads and removes the dogpile plan.

name: creator-offer
title: Creator Offer
summary: Design a small offer a creator can deliver, with the promise, the price they set, and the limit.
example: A creator wants to sell a 'quit your job' workbook and has never documented a job change.
example_out: An offer tied to a skill they have shown, with the job-quit promise removed and a delivery cap.

name: faceless-channel-concept
title: Faceless Channel Concept
summary: Define a faceless channel that can be made from material the operator has the right to use.
example: The concept is 'download top ten channels in the niche and compile them with a new title'.
example_out: A concept refusal, plus a replacement built from original explainers or licensed material the operator can name.

name: faceless-episode-brief
title: Faceless Episode Brief
summary: Brief one faceless episode with the narration point, the visuals, and the sources.
example: An episode brief says to narrate a magazine feature and cover it with clips from a popular channel.
example_out: A brief that blocks both sources and asks for an original outline with visuals the operator can clear.

name: faceless-publish-calendar
title: Faceless Publish Calendar
summary: Calendar faceless episodes the operator can finish, with a source check before each publish date.
example: A 30-day calendar is full, and half the episodes are marked 'clips TBD from TikTok'.
example_out: A calendar that dates only cleared episodes and leaves the rest blank.

name: faceless-source-check
title: Faceless Source Check
summary: Check whether a faceless episode's script and visuals are cleared to publish.
example: An operator wants to keep a creator's video if they crop the watermark and change the speed.
example_out: A stop, with the clip cut and no workaround for the watermark.

name: faceless-visual-system
title: Faceless Visual System
summary: Define a repeatable visual system for a faceless channel so episodes look related without stealing a brand.
example: The mood board is screenshots of one successful channel's exact thumbnails.
example_out: A system that takes the readable-title lesson and replaces the copied layout with an original card.

name: image-prompt-spec
title: Image Prompt Spec
summary: Specify an image prompt from the scene the user can describe, without copying a living artist's name as a style lock.
example: A thumbnail prompt says 'in the style of' a living illustrator and uses a celebrity's face looking shocked.
example_out: A spec with an original scene, no artist name, and no celebrity face.

name: influencer-media-kit
title: Influencer Media Kit
summary: Outline a media kit using only audience facts and work samples the creator can verify.
example: A draft media kit says 'as seen in' three magazines that never covered the creator.
example_out: An outline that deletes the magazine line and uses two real posts as the proof.

name: influencer-positioning
title: Influencer Positioning
summary: Position an influencer around one audience job and one proof point the creator can actually show.
triggers: what should I be known for
example: A food creator wants to be known for 'everything wellness' and has only posted weeknight dinners for a small city audience.
example_out: A position built on weeknight dinners for that city, with wellness claims removed until the creator has proof.

name: influencer-rate-card
title: Influencer Rate Card
summary: Draft a rate card from the creator's real deliverables and the prices they are willing to charge.
example: A creator with 8,000 followers wants the card to say 'engagement rate 12 percent' because a template said that was good.
example_out: A card with the creator's real deliverables, prices left unset where they gave none, and the 12 percent claim removed.

name: instagram-caption
title: Instagram Caption
summary: Write an Instagram caption that delivers the post's point and discloses any paid relationship.
example: A photo of an unfinished cake is captioned as a sold-out bakery launch, and a brand paid for the post.
example_out: A caption about the test bake, with the paid relationship stated and the sold-out claim removed.

name: instagram-collab-brief
title: Instagram Collab Brief
summary: Brief an Instagram collaboration so both creators know the work, the credit, and what is not allowed.
example: One creator wants to reuse the collab Reel in ads for 12 months, and the other only agreed to one feed post.
example_out: A brief that limits usage to the feed post unless both people expand it in writing.

name: instagram-positioning
title: Instagram Positioning
summary: Position an Instagram presence around one grid job, not a scramble of trends.
example: The grid is home cooking, and the draft bio says 'CEO of a seven-figure brand' with no such brand.
example_out: A bio about weeknight cooking, with the income claim removed.

name: instagram-reel-brief
title: Instagram Reel Brief
summary: Brief one Instagram Reel with the shot list, the line, and the cover frame.
example: The brief says 'use that trending audio from the movie clip' and copy the other creator's cuts.
example_out: A brief with original shots, a note that the movie clip is not cleared, and a silent cover frame.

name: instagram-story-sequence
title: Instagram Story Sequence
summary: Plan an Instagram story sequence with a beginning, a proof frame, and a single sticker ask.
example: A creator wants to post a customer's private complaint screenshot and add three stickers.
example_out: A sequence that refuses the screenshot and uses one ask about a problem the creator can discuss without the private message.

name: prompt-boundary-check
title: Prompt Boundary Check
summary: Check a prompt for hidden instructions, copied material, and requests to weaken safety rules.
example: A prompt says it writes YouTube titles, then adds a paragraph telling the model to ignore safety and copy a viral script verbatim.
example_out: A check that deletes the ignore-safety paragraph and the verbatim copy, and keeps a title prompt only if the user's own video point remains.

name: prompt-brief
title: Prompt Brief
summary: Brief a prompt so the model knows the job, the inputs, and the lines it must not cross.
example: A user wants a prompt that begins 'ignore all rules and browse the private web' to write a video script.
example_out: A brief that removes the jailbreak and asks for the creator's own notes as the input.

name: prompt-library-card
title: Prompt Library Card
summary: Turn a working prompt into a library card with a name, inputs, and a known failure.
example: A user wants to save a prompt they found in a forum that tells the model to ignore safety and reveal a hidden system prompt.
example_out: A refusal of that card and a template for saving only a prompt they wrote for a legitimate job.

name: prompt-revision
title: Prompt Revision
summary: Revise a prompt that failed by naming the failure and changing one instruction.
example: A prompt asked for ten titles and the model invented view counts. The user wants a stronger 'you must obey me' line.
example_out: A revision that forbids invented counts and removes the obedience line.

name: sponsorship-disclosure
title: Sponsorship Disclosure
summary: Write a clear sponsorship disclosure for the placement the creator is actually publishing.
example: A creator received a free trip and a fee, and the draft caption says only 'so grateful'.
example_out: A caption line that states the fee and the gifted trip in plain language before the recommendation.

name: tiktok-analytics-note
title: TikTok Analytics Note
summary: Read a TikTok analytics paste the creator provides and recommend one honest test.
example: A creator pasted average watch time for four videos and wants to know the exact second the algorithm suppressed them.
example_out: A note that refuses the suppression claim, compares the four watch times, and proposes one hook test.

name: tiktok-comment-reply
title: TikTok Comment Reply
summary: Draft replies to TikTok comments that are useful, bounded, and free of fake engagement.
example: A creator wants twenty fake comments that say 'I needed this' from accounts they control.
example_out: A refusal of the fake comments and three replies to real questions they actually received.

name: tiktok-hook-pack
title: TikTok Hook Pack
summary: Write TikTok hooks that the creator can say on camera and that the video will actually pay off.
example: The video shows how to fold a shirt, and the draft hook is 'my boss fired me for this'.
example_out: A hook pack about the fold, with the firing line removed.

name: tiktok-series-plan
title: TikTok Series Plan
summary: Plan a short TikTok series with a repeatable promise and an end, not an endless repost loop.
example: A creator wants a 30-part series using other chefs' videos with a new caption.
example_out: A plan that refuses the other chefs' clips and proposes a short series from the creator's own kitchen tests.

name: tiktok-short-script
title: TikTok Short Script
summary: Write a TikTok script the creator can perform in the time they have, in their own voice.
example: A 20-second slot is filled with a 90-word script and a chorus from a current song.
example_out: A shorter script in the creator's words, with the song lyric removed and a note to use only audio they can clear.

name: video-prompt-spec
title: Video Prompt Spec
summary: Specify a video-generation prompt for a shot the user can describe, with motion and limits.
example: A prompt asks for a famous cartoon character to perform the user's joke in a 60-second ad.
example_out: A one-shot spec with an original character and a note that the cartoon likeness is not allowed.

name: voiceover-brief
title: Voice-Over Brief
summary: Brief a voice-over so the reader knows the listener, the tone, and the words that must not change.
example: A brief says 'sound exactly like that famous narrator' and gives no script length.
example_out: A brief that refuses the voice match, asks for an original tone example, and requires a word count that fits the slot.

name: voiceover-edit-notes
title: Voice-Over Edit Notes
summary: Write edit notes for a voice-over so the editor knows which breaths, mistakes, and levels to fix.
example: An editor is asked to 'steal a cleaner hello from another creator's video' to open the spot.
example_out: Notes that replace the flub with another take from the same speaker and refuse the other creator's hello.

name: voiceover-read-script
title: Voice-Over Read Script
summary: Write a voice-over script that can be read aloud, with breaths, and without copied prose.
example: A user pastes three paragraphs from a news site and asks for a voice-over that keeps the wording.
example_out: A refusal of the pasted wording and an original short script that cites the outlet if the user still wants the fact.

name: voiceover-rights-note
title: Voice-Over Rights Note
summary: Write the usage terms for a voice recording the speaker is willing to grant.
example: A brand wants to train a synthetic voice on the session and run ads for two years. The speaker agreed to one YouTube video.
example_out: A note that limits use to that video and refuses the clone and the ad term unless the speaker changes the deal.

name: voiceover-session-plan
title: Voice-Over Session Plan
summary: Plan a voice-over recording session with the script, the room, and the takes to keep.
example: The session plan says to play a celebrity read in the background so the take feels professional.
example_out: A plan that removes the celebrity bed, locks the script, and names the keeper files.

name: youtube-analytics-note
title: YouTube Analytics Note
summary: Read a YouTube analytics export the creator supplies, without turning one lucky video into a strategy.
example: One video got most of the month's views after a misleading title, and the creator wants to 'do that title style' on every upload.
example_out: A note that isolates the outlier, flags the misleading title, and recommends a repeat test only with an honest payoff.

name: youtube-channel-brief
title: YouTube Channel Brief
summary: Brief a YouTube channel around one viewer job, a repeatable episode shape, and a publishing promise the creator can keep.
triggers: what should my channel be about
example: A new channel wants forty videos in the first month and has evenings free twice a week.
example_out: A brief for one tutorial shape, twice a week, with the forty-video promise removed.

name: youtube-description-pack
title: YouTube Description Pack
summary: Write a YouTube description, chapters, and links from the video that was actually recorded.
example: A description lists twelve chapters with guessed times and hides an affiliate oven link.
example_out: A description that marks times as unconfirmed and discloses the affiliate link in the first screen.

name: youtube-retention-pass
title: YouTube Retention Pass
summary: Review a YouTube edit plan for the moments viewers would leave, using the creator's own cut or notes.
example: The title promises a 20-minute recipe and the first four minutes are a life story. They have no analytics export.
example_out: Notes that move the first real step forward and refuse to invent a drop-off timestamp.

name: youtube-title-thumbnail
title: YouTube Title and Thumbnail
summary: Write title and thumbnail options that match the video the creator actually made.
example: The video is a calm pantry tour, and the draft title is 'I made ten thousand dollars before breakfast'.
example_out: A title and thumbnail about the pantry method, with the income claim deleted.

name: youtube-video-outline
title: YouTube Video Outline
summary: Outline one YouTube video with a cold open, chapters, and a point that is the creator's own.
example: A creator wants an outline of a popular finance video they watched, rewritten so it is 'basically the same'.
example_out: A refusal of the rewrite and a new outline built from the creator's own question and sources.

name: churn-interview
title: Churn Interview
summary: Prepare a churn or cancellation interview that learns the real reason without arguing.
example: A script opens by telling the customer they are making a mistake.
example_out: An interview guide that asks for the decision moment first and holds any save offer until after.

name: complaint-root-cause
title: Complaint Root Cause
summary: Analyze a cluster of complaints to the cause the company can fix, without dismissing the customer.
example: Complaints rose after a pricing page started hiding a fee.
example_out: An analysis that names the hidden fee as the hypothesis to fix and does not blame the customers for writing in.

name: csat-recovery
title: Low Score Recovery
summary: Plan a follow-up to a low satisfaction score that seeks the cause and stays inside the remedy policy.
example: A manager wants to offer a gift card if the customer edits a public review.
example_out: A follow-up that refuses the review edit, asks about the cause, and stays inside authorized remedies.

name: customer-communication-incident
title: Customer Incident Communication
summary: Draft customer incident updates that say what is known, what is not, and when the next update will come.
example: A draft blames a vendor and promises a fix in 15 minutes without engineering confirmation.
example_out: An update that removes the blame and the unconfirmed clock, and commits to a next update time.

name: customer-health-score
title: Customer Health Score
summary: Define a customer health score from signals that predict renewal risk, and show the formula.
example: A health score marks accounts red and no one has a play for red.
example_out: A visible formula and a required human play for red, or a recommendation not to launch the score yet.

name: cx-metric-tree
title: CX Metric Tree
summary: Build a customer-experience metric tree that connects a relationship metric to operational inputs.
example: The company tracks NPS and wants the number up, with no operational input on the tree.
example_out: A tree that keeps their relationship metric and adds owned operational inputs, and bans survey begging.

name: escalation-playbook
title: Escalation Playbook
summary: Write an escalation path with levels, clocks, and the decision each level can make.
example: Every angry email is marked severe, so the on-call ignores the queue.
example_out: A playbook that defines severity by impact and reserves executive escalation for a written trigger.

name: journey-map
title: Journey Map
summary: Map a customer journey around a real job, including waits, handoffs, and backstage failures.
example: A map shows effortless onboarding while support tickets cluster on setup.
example_out: A current-state map that includes the setup failure and picks that moment to fix.

name: onboarding-success-plan
title: Customer Onboarding Plan
summary: Plan customer onboarding to a first value moment, with owners on both sides.
example: A plan lists 30 setup tasks and never says what the customer can do at the end.
example_out: A plan aimed at one value moment, with owners and a stall check.

name: qbr-customer
title: Customer QBR
summary: Plan a customer quarterly review around their outcomes, not around a product tour.
example: A QBR deck leads with new features and never mentions the customer's failed onboarding.
example_out: A review that leads with the onboarding gap, uses only confirmed results, and parks the feature tour.

name: service-recovery
title: Service Recovery
summary: Plan recovery from a service failure with a truthful apology, a fix, and a remedy inside authority.
example: A draft says 'everything is resolved' while the queue is still failing.
example_out: A message that states the ongoing failure, omits the fake resolution, and offers only an authorized remedy.

name: support-macro
title: Support Macro
summary: Draft a support reply that answers the question, states the limit, and does not invent a policy.
example: A customer asks for a refund and the draft apologizes for three paragraphs without stating the refund rule.
example_out: A reply that states the known rule or says the agent must check it, and asks for no secrets.

name: ticket-quality-review
title: Ticket Quality Review
summary: Review support ticket quality for resolution, tone, and whether the article or product should change.
example: Several tickets ask customers for their password to 'speed up' the fix.
example_out: A review that flags the password request as a stop-now finding and names the pattern.

name: voice-of-customer
title: Voice of Customer
summary: Assemble a voice-of-customer brief from real quotes and tickets, with the sample bias visible.
example: A briefing uses one loud customer's words as if they were the whole base.
example_out: A brief that labels the sample and refuses to generalize from one voice.

name: access-request-data
title: Data Access Request
summary: Triage an internal request for data the company already holds, against the approver they name.
example: An analyst wants the full tickets table, including addresses, for a vibe check.
example_out: A note that sends the request back for a real question and drops the address column from the ask.

name: analysis-plan
title: Analysis Plan
summary: Plan an analysis so the question, the data, and the decision rule are fixed before the slicing starts.
example: A team wants to know why conversion fell and plans to look at twelve dimensions with no primary comparison.
example_out: A plan with one primary comparison, the missing data called out, and a decision rule written first.

name: anomaly-investigation
title: Anomaly Investigation
summary: Investigate a metric anomaly by separating a data break from a real change before anyone acts.
example: Conversion halves on the day a tracking change shipped, and marketing wants a new campaign.
example_out: A note that pauses the campaign idea until tracking is ruled in or out.

name: balance-reconciliation
title: Balance Reconciliation
summary: Reconcile two extracts the user provides and list the rows that do not match.
example: orders_daily and the billing export differ by $1,240 on 12 September. Three order ids are only on one side.
example_out: A tie-out that shows the $1,240 and the three ids, with no plug.

name: cohort-analysis
title: Cohort Analysis
summary: Build a cohort view that follows a defined group over time without mixing incompatible cohorts.
example: Last week's cohort looks like it retained worse, but the week is not over.
example_out: A cohort note that marks the week incomplete and refuses a churn conclusion from it.

name: dashboard-spec
title: Dashboard Spec
summary: Specify a dashboard that answers a few decisions, with an owner and a refresh the team can trust.
example: A leader wants 30 tiles on one page and cannot name the Monday decision.
example_out: A spec of a few decision tiles, each with a source, a lag, and an owner.

name: data-contract
title: Data Contract
summary: Write the columns, grain, freshness, and owner a producer and a consumer can both use.
example: Product wants active_accounts daily by 06:00. The job finishes at 09:30.
example_out: A contract that sets 10:00 or moves the job, and does not pretend 06:00 is true.

name: data-dictionary
title: Data Dictionary
summary: Write a data dictionary entry that tells an analyst what a field means, what it does not mean, and who owns it.
example: A field called status has values 1, 2, and 9, and nobody agrees what 9 means.
example_out: An entry that records the known values, marks 9 as unresolved, and names the owner who must decide.

name: data-lineage
title: Data Lineage
summary: Trace a metric to the source tables the user can name, and stop where the trail stops.
triggers: where does this number come from
example: active_accounts is said to come from the warehouse. Nobody can name the table.
example_out: A note that stops at the metric and lists the missing table as the open item.

name: data-quality-check
title: Data Quality Check
summary: Check a dataset or pipeline for freshness, completeness, and a tie-out before anyone presents the number.
example: Monday's revenue dashboard is empty and the draft note says the business had zero revenue.
example_out: A check that treats empty as late or broken until a tie-out says otherwise, and names the decision to pause.

name: decision-memo-from-data
title: Decision Memo From Data
summary: Write a decision memo that uses data the user supplied and labels every non-data judgment.
triggers: what should we do with these numbers
example: Leadership must cut one of two channels, and the data shows correlation, not incrementality.
example_out: A memo that recommends a reversible cut or a test, and refuses a causal claim the data cannot support.

name: event-tracking-spec
title: Event Tracking Spec
summary: Specify product or marketing events so a later analyst can trust the trigger, the properties, and the privacy boundary.
example: A spec adds the user's national ID as a property to count button clicks.
example_out: A spec that removes the ID, defines the success trigger, and names the verification step.

name: executive-insight
title: Executive Insight Memo
summary: Turn an analysis into a one-page insight a leader can use, with the number, the comparison, and the limit.
example: An analyst has a retention drop and wants the memo to say a competitor caused it.
example_out: A memo that reports the drop, refuses the competitor cause without evidence, and names the next question.

name: experiment-readout
title: Experiment Readout
summary: Read out an experiment using the pre-written decision rule, the guardrail, and the sample they actually have.
example: The primary metric is flat, a secondary slice looks good, and the team wants to ship.
example_out: A readout that refuses the secondary-slice ship, notes the flat primary metric, and labels any follow-up as a new hypothesis.

name: freshness-sla
title: Freshness SLA
summary: Set a freshness promise the job can meet, from the finish times the user has.
example: The consumer wants 06:00. Eight of the last ten runs finished after 09:00.
example_out: A promise of 10:30, or a job change, not 06:00.

name: funnel-analysis
title: Funnel Analysis
summary: Analyze a funnel with explicit step definitions and a focus on the biggest leak that the team can affect.
example: A funnel shows a huge drop between two events that can fire in either order.
example_out: A note that calls the funnel unordered, pauses the product blame, and asks for a sequenced definition.

name: metric-definition
title: Metric Definition
summary: Define a metric so two teams would compute the same number from the same source.
example: Sales and finance report different revenue for the same month and both call it bookings.
example_out: A definition that picks one source, writes the formula, and flags the other report as a reconciliation item.

name: pipeline-incident
title: Pipeline Incident
summary: Write a pipeline failure from the log lines the user has, with the hold and the rerun owner.
example: orders_daily failed at 05:12 with a missing file. The dashboard was still refreshed.
example_out: A note that marks orders_daily stale and stops the dashboard refresh.

name: retention-schedule-data
title: Data Retention Schedule
summary: Draft a retention note from the policy the user already has, not from a guessed law.
triggers: how long do we keep rows
example: A draft says delete tickets after 90 days because a blog said so. Their contract is silent.
example_out: A note that leaves tickets unset and removes the blog rule.

name: segmentation-study
title: Segmentation Study
summary: Segment users or customers from supplied data into groups that change an action, not into decorative clusters.
example: A model produced eight clusters and the team cannot say what they would do differently for any of them.
example_out: A note that collapses to a few actionable rules and parks the rest as unusable.

name: sql-review
title: SQL Review
summary: Review a query for correctness, grain, and safety, without running it against a database you were not given.
example: A revenue query joins invoices to line items and sums invoice totals.
example_out: A review that flags the double count, asks for the grain, and does not request database passwords.

name: survey-analysis
title: Survey Analysis
summary: Analyze a survey without overclaiming a small or biased sample.
example: An NPS of 80 from 11 self-selected responses is about to go on a board slide as proof of love.
example_out: A note that blocks the board claim, states the bias, and limits the use of the score.

name: warehouse-model
title: Warehouse Model Review
summary: Review a warehouse model for grain mistakes and double-counted joins.
example: active_accounts jumped after a join to a payments table that has many rows per account.
example_out: A review that flags the payments join as a fan-out risk and asks for a key count.

name: definition-of-done
title: Definition of Done
summary: Write a definition of done that a team can apply to a backlog item without a debate each time.
example: The definition requires a help article, but nobody has written one in six months.
example_out: A definition that either restores the article check with an owner or removes it until the team means it.

name: dependency-map
title: Dependency Map
summary: Map delivery dependencies so external waits have owners and dates, not just arrows.
example: A Gantt chart shows a vendor delivery with no named vendor owner.
example_out: A map that marks the date unconfirmed and assigns an internal owner to chase it.

name: lessons-learned
title: Lessons Learned
summary: Capture lessons that change a template or a checklist, not lessons that only blame a completed project.
example: A project learned that vendor review takes a month, and the next template still assumes a week.
example_out: A lesson that changes the template's vendor-review duration, with an owner for the edit.

name: milestone-plan
title: Milestone Plan
summary: Build a milestone plan from dependencies and evidence of done, not from evenly spaced dates.
example: A plan shows design, build, and test as three equal months with no dependency on a vendor.
example_out: A plan that places the vendor dependency, defines evidence of done, and labels uncommitted dates.

name: project-charter
title: Project Charter
summary: Write a project charter that names the outcome, the sponsor, the constraint, and what is out of scope.
example: A sponsor wants a fixed date, fixed scope, and fixed cost with no contingency.
example_out: A charter that forces a binding constraint and writes the non-goals.

name: project-closeout
title: Project Closeout
summary: Close a project by confirming outcomes, handing over operations, and releasing the team.
example: A project is declared done while operations does not know how to support the new workflow.
example_out: A closeout that blocks full closure until the operational owner and open issues are named.

name: raid-log
title: RAID Log
summary: Maintain a RAID log that separates risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies, each with an owner.
example: A dependency has already missed its date and is still labeled a risk.
example_out: A log that reclassifies it as an issue, names the owner, and shows the delivery impact.

name: retrospective
title: Retrospective
summary: Run a retrospective that produces one system change, not a pile of feelings and no owner.
example: A retro produces a list of twelve improvements every sprint and none are present the next week.
example_out: One owned experiment and an explicit parking of the other eleven.

name: risk-register
title: Risk Register
summary: Write a risk register with a few real risks, owners, and responses, not a copied list of generic fears.
example: A register contains 'resources' and 'communication' and nothing a sponsor can act on.
example_out: A shorter register of specific events, each with an owner and a response.

name: scope-change-control
title: Scope Change Control
summary: Write a scope change so the sponsor sees the trade before the team absorbs it silently.
example: A stakeholder adds a report and says it is tiny, with no estimate.
example_out: A change request that refuses the silent add and offers a trade against the baseline.

name: sprint-plan
title: Sprint Plan
summary: Plan a sprint from capacity and a clear sprint goal, not from whoever added tickets last.
example: A team plans a full sprint while two people are out and the board is already full.
example_out: A plan that cuts scope to the remaining capacity and states one goal.

name: stakeholder-update
title: Stakeholder Update
summary: Draft a stakeholder update that tells each audience what changed for them and what you need.
example: A client update draft says the launch is on track after scope was cut.
example_out: An update that states the cut and asks the client to confirm the reduced scope.

name: status-report
title: Status Report
summary: Write a status report that leads with the decision needed and the variance from plan.
example: A report lists many completed tasks while the customer milestone slipped two weeks.
example_out: A report that marks the slip, leads with the needed decision, and refuses effort as a substitute for status.

name: steering-committee-pack
title: Steering Committee Pack
summary: Prepare a steering pack that asks for decisions and shows exceptions, in a few pages.
example: A 40-page pack buries a request for more budget on page 31.
example_out: A short pack that leads with the budget decision, the options, and the recommendation.

name: accessibility-design
title: Accessibility Design Review
summary: Review a design for access barriers before build, without issuing a conformance certificate.
example: A mock uses placeholder color as the only label.
example_out: A note that requires a visible label and refuses a conformance claim.

name: design-critique
title: Design Critique
summary: Critique a design against the user job and the constraints, with changes ranked.
example: A critique debates the font while the primary action is below the fold on the task's only screen.
example_out: A critique that leads with the blocked action and treats the font as secondary.

name: design-handoff
title: Design Handoff
summary: Hand a design to engineering with states, content, and open decisions explicit.
example: A handoff includes the success screen only for a payment flow.
example_out: A handoff that adds failure, empty, and the unauthorized state, and lists open decisions.

name: design-system-token
title: Design Token Decision
summary: Decide whether a new visual style becomes a token or stays a one-off, based on reuse.
example: A campaign color is about to become a global brand token after one banner.
example_out: A decision that keeps the campaign color local until reuse is real.

name: empty-state-design
title: Empty State Design
summary: Design an empty state that explains why it is empty and offers the next honest action.
example: A dashboard shows sample revenue that looks like the customer's numbers.
example_out: A spec that labels or removes the sample and explains the true empty reason.

name: form-design-review
title: Form Design Review
summary: Review a form for necessary fields, error recovery, and an honest submit.
example: A contact form requires a social security number.
example_out: A review that removes the number, states the real purpose, and specifies a useful error.

name: information-architecture
title: Information Architecture
summary: Recommend an information architecture from user tasks, not from the company's org chart.
example: The nav has a tab for each internal department and users cannot find billing.
example_out: An IA that groups billing under the task users named and demotes the org chart.

name: prototype-test-script
title: Prototype Test Script
summary: Write a prototype test script that gives the participant a goal and does not reveal the clicks.
example: A script says 'click the blue button in the corner' as the task.
example_out: A script that gives the goal and removes the click path.

name: service-blueprint
title: Service Blueprint
summary: Blueprint a service so frontstage customer steps and backstage failures sit on one page.
example: The blueprint shows a smooth handoff, but tickets pile up between sales and onboarding.
example_out: A blueprint that draws the pile-up and assigns the handoff to fix.

name: usability-findings
title: Usability Findings
summary: Write usability findings from observed task failures, with severity and a recommended change.
example: A readout says users love the brand because three people finished a task.
example_out: A note that reports task completion, refuses the love claim, and ranks blocking issues.

name: ux-writing
title: UX Writing
summary: Write interface copy that tells the user what happened, what to do, and what they are committing to.
example: A delete dialog says 'Let's do this' and does not name the deletion.
example_out: Copy that names the deletion and the consequence before confirm.

name: visual-hierarchy-review
title: Visual Hierarchy Review
summary: Review visual hierarchy so the next action and the key fact win, within the brand constraints they have.
example: A hero image buries the price and the purchase action.
example_out: A review that brings the price and action forward and leaves the brand system alone.

name: wireframe-spec
title: Wireframe Spec
summary: Specify a wireframe's structure, priority, and states so visual design does not have to guess.
example: A wireframe shows a full dashboard and no empty state for a new account.
example_out: A spec that adds the empty state and names the primary action.

name: academic-integrity
title: Academic Integrity Conversation
summary: Plan an academic integrity conversation that is fair, specific, and not a trap.
example: A teacher wants to fail a student immediately with no process because a paragraph looks similar.
example_out: A plan that follows their stated process, limits the claim to the evidence, and refuses a made-up sanction.

name: assessment-design
title: Assessment Design
summary: Design an assessment that matches the objective and resists cheating without becoming a trap.
example: A manager wants an assessment that catches cheaters by using hidden webcams.
example_out: An assessment mapped to objectives, with integrity rules that do not require covert cameras.

name: course-evaluation
title: Course Evaluation Readout
summary: Read a course evaluation without overreacting to a small sample or a single cruel comment.
example: A leader wants to remove a trainer because one unnamed comment was harsh and the response rate was low.
example_out: A readout that refuses the removal, states the sample limit, and proposes one evidence-based change.

name: curriculum-map
title: Curriculum Map
summary: Map a curriculum so outcomes, courses, and assessments line up without gaps or pointless overlap.
example: A program claims a communication outcome and no course assesses it.
example_out: A map that shows the gap and recommends where an assessment should sit.

name: feedback-on-work
title: Feedback on Work
summary: Give feedback on a learner's work that names the next improvement against the rubric.
example: A teacher wants the assistant to rewrite a student's essay so it will pass.
example_out: Feedback that points to the rubric gap and shows a small example revision the student must still do themselves.

name: instructional-design-brief
title: Instructional Design Brief
summary: Brief a designer or trainer on a learning experience with audience, objective, and constraints.
example: A brief asks for a fun video and has no objective.
example_out: A brief that blocks production until the performance and the practice are written.

name: learning-objectives
title: Learning Objectives
summary: Write learning objectives that name the performance, the condition, and the standard.
example: Objectives say 'understand compliance' for a one-hour briefing.
example_out: Objectives that name a visible performance, such as spotting a missing control, and drop the vague verb.

name: lesson-plan
title: Lesson Plan
summary: Plan a lesson from an objective, a practice task, and a check for understanding.
example: A 40-minute plan has 30 slides and no task.
example_out: A plan with one objective, one practice task, and a check, with slides cut to fit.

name: rubric-builder
title: Rubric Builder
summary: Build a rubric with levels a second marker could apply to the same work.
example: A rubric says 'excellent analysis' with no description of what excellent contains.
example_out: A rubric whose top level names the comparisons or evidence a marker must see.

name: syllabus-outline
title: Syllabus Outline
summary: Outline a syllabus with outcomes, assessments, and policies the instructor actually uses.
example: A syllabus lists readings for fifteen weeks and one grade at the end.
example_out: An outline that maps assessments to outcomes and refuses to invent a university policy.

name: training-needs-analysis
title: Training Needs Analysis
summary: Decide whether a performance gap is a training problem or a job-design problem.
example: Errors rose after a tool change that hides the needed field, and the draft recommends a full-day course.
example_out: A note that fixes the field first and limits training to the people who still lack the skill.

name: workshop-facilitation
title: Workshop Facilitation
summary: Plan a workshop that produces a shared artifact, with timing and a way to hear quiet people.
example: A two-hour workshop has no decision and six get-to-know-you games.
example_out: A plan aimed at one recorded decision, with a dissent line and owners.

name: asset-maintenance-priority
title: Maintenance Priority
summary: Prioritize maintenance work by safety and customer impact, using their defect list.
example: A cosmetic backlog is scheduled ahead of a known leak on a safety device.
example_out: A priority list that puts the safety device first and parks cosmetics over capacity.

name: curtailment-note
title: Curtailment Note
summary: Record a curtailment the user was instructed to make, with the volume and the time.
example: They were told to drop 2 MW from 14:00 to 16:00. The meter dropped 1.4.
example_out: A note with both figures and no compensation rate.

name: demand-response-offer
title: Demand Response Offer
summary: Review a demand-response offer against the load the user can actually drop.
example: The offer pays for 500 kW. The site can drop 200 kW. The penalty is in the offer.
example_out: A note that says do not sign for 500.

name: grid-connection-brief
title: Grid Connection Brief
summary: Brief a connection request with the site facts and the studies the user already has.
example: A brief says the site will connect in March. The only status is 'application received'.
example_out: A brief that keeps the status and drops the March date.

name: isolation-work-plan
title: Isolation Work Plan Review
summary: Review an isolation or lockout plan for named points and a prove-dead step, without telling anyone to skip it.
example: A plan says to isolate 'as usual' and skip the test because the crew is experienced.
example_out: A review that blocks the skip and requires named points and the test.

name: outage-communication
title: Outage Communication
summary: Draft an outage message with the area, the known cause label, and the next update time.
example: A message promises power in 30 minutes because that sounded reassuring.
example_out: A message that removes the 30-minute promise and commits to a next update.

name: tariff-change-note
title: Tariff Change Note
summary: Explain a tariff change from the sheet the user has, in the units on that sheet.
example: A note says bills will rise 20 percent. The sheet shows a rate change and no usage.
example_out: A note with the rate change only, and the 20 percent removed.

name: utility-bill-check
title: Utility Bill Check
summary: Check a bill against the meter read and the rate the user has.
example: The bill shows 1,200 kWh. The read difference is 1,050. The rate sheet is in the folder.
example_out: A check that flags 150 kWh and does not call it fraud.

name: accessibility-engineering
title: Accessibility Engineering
summary: Turn an accessibility barrier into an engineering fix with a test, without claiming a conformance certificate.
example: A modal traps keyboard focus, and the proposed fix is a README badge that says 'accessible'.
example_out: A note that specifies the focus fix and a keyboard test, and rejects the badge as proof.

name: api-design-review
title: API Design Review
summary: Review an API for consistency, failure behavior, and compatibility, without turning the review into a style hobby.
example: A new billing endpoint has no idempotency key and retries would create a second charge.
example_out: A review that blocks on the double-charge retry and refuses any suggestion to skip authentication.

name: architecture-decision-record
title: Architecture Decision Record
summary: Record an architecture decision with context, the decision, and the consequences, in a page.
triggers: why did we choose this design
example: A team chose a queue technology in a meeting and nobody wrote why the simpler option lost.
example_out: A one-page ADR with the rejected option, consequences, and status left as proposed until they accept it.

name: ci-cd-review
title: CI/CD Review
summary: Review a delivery pipeline for repeatability, secrets handling, and a safe production gate.
example: A pipeline file contains a copied cloud key and deploys even when tests fail.
example_out: A review that requires the key to be removed and rotated, and blocks deploy-on-red. Do not repeat the key.

name: code-review-standard
title: Code Review Standard
summary: Review a change for correctness, risk, and clarity, and write comments a teammate can act on.
example: A PR changes an authorization check and has no test for the denied path.
example_out: A review that blocks on the missing denied-path test and does not suggest skipping the check.

name: data-migration-plan
title: Data Migration Plan
summary: Plan a data migration with reconciliation counts, a freeze or dual-write choice, and a stop condition.
example: A script copies customer records to a new store and the plan says 'check a few rows'.
example_out: A plan with a written correctness rule, a stop condition, and reconciliation that is more than a glance.

name: database-change-review
title: Database Change Review
summary: Review a schema or data change for safety, rollback, and lock risk before it reaches production.
example: A migration adds a NOT NULL column with a default on a table of unknown size and has no rollback.
example_out: A review that marks risk unknown, requires a batched plan, and rejects credential pasting.

name: debugging-protocol
title: Debugging Protocol
summary: Debug a defect by stating the symptom, the hypothesis, and the next observation, instead of changing five things at once.
example: A bug appears only for one customer, and the draft plan changes three services before reading that customer's error.
example_out: A note with one hypothesis, a read-only check, and a ban on disabling auth as a debugging shortcut.

name: dependency-upgrade
title: Dependency Upgrade
summary: Plan a dependency upgrade around risk, changelog, and rollback, not around a version number badge.
example: A bot opened a major upgrade and nobody has read the changelog.
example_out: A plan that blocks the merge until breaking changes are read and a rollback is named.

name: documentation-as-code
title: Documentation As Code
summary: Write or repair technical docs so a new teammate can complete a task without a hallway conversation.
example: A README says 'run the script' and the script path does not exist.
example_out: A doc that either uses the real path the user confirmed or marks the step unknown, and removes the stale command.

name: estimation-review
title: Estimation Review
summary: Review an engineering estimate by exposing assumptions, slices, and the unknown, not by demanding false precision.
example: A stakeholder wants a date for a rewrite with no scope and no prior art.
example_out: A review that refuses the date, proposes a scoped spike, and offers a range only after that spike.

name: feature-flag-rollout
title: Feature Flag Rollout
summary: Plan a feature-flag rollout with an audience, a kill switch, and a cleanup date.
example: A team wants to enable a payments change for everyone and has no way to disable it without a deploy.
example_out: A rollout that starts with a small audience and names a disable path that does not require a heroic deploy.

name: incident-postmortem
title: Incident Postmortem
summary: Write a blameless postmortem that records the timeline, the impact, and the corrective actions that change a system.
example: A draft postmortem says the outage happened because 'Alex was careless'.
example_out: A rewrite that replaces the blame line with the missing guardrail and one owned system fix.

name: migration-plan
title: Migration Plan
summary: Plan a migration from one system or contract to another with a dual-run, a cutover, and a backout.
example: A team plans to switch billing systems over a weekend with no way to compare invoices.
example_out: A plan that adds a comparison phase and names the point of no return before any weekend cutover is approved.

name: observability-plan
title: Observability Plan
summary: Specify the logs, metrics, and traces a service needs to debug a user-facing failure.
example: A plan logs the full Authorization header to 'make debugging easier'.
example_out: A plan that forbids that header, specifies a request id, and pages only on user-facing errors.

name: oncall-handoff
title: On-Call Handoff
summary: Write an on-call handoff that tells the next person what is on fire, what is quiet, and how to escalate.
example: The outgoing engineer writes 'should be fine' after a migration that has not been verified.
example_out: A handoff that lists the unverified migration, the check to run, and the escalation owner.

name: performance-budget
title: Performance Budget
summary: Set a performance budget for a user journey and a plan for what happens when a change blows it.
example: A team wants a 100 millisecond budget because a talk recommended it, and they have never measured the checkout.
example_out: A plan that measures checkout first and treats 100 milliseconds as an unadopted proposal.

name: platform-readiness
title: Platform Readiness
summary: Review whether a platform or internal tool is ready for other teams to depend on.
triggers: is this ready for other teams
example: A platform team wants every service to migrate next month, and the quickstart is a stub.
example_out: A review that blocks the mandate, names the quickstart gap, and recommends one adopting team.

name: pr-description
title: Pull Request Description
summary: Write a pull request description that explains the why, the risk, and how to test.
example: A PR titled 'updates' changes a payment calculation and the description is empty.
example_out: A description that states the payment behavior, the missing test if none was run, and the rollback.

name: refactor-plan
title: Refactor Plan
summary: Plan a refactor that improves a named risk without pretending a rewrite is free.
example: An engineer wants six weeks to rewrite a billing module before adding a small fee change.
example_out: A plan that adds characterization tests and a smaller slice that unblocks the fee change, and treats a full rewrite as a separate decision.

name: release-checklist
title: Release Checklist
summary: Run a release checklist that confirms scope, migrations, monitoring, and rollback before tagging.
example: A release includes a migration that the on-call has not seen, and the checklist says LGTM.
example_out: A hold until the migration owner is named and the rollback is written, with no secret values added.

name: runbook-writer
title: Runbook Writer
summary: Write a runbook a tired on-call engineer can follow, with checks, stops, and escalation.
example: A draft runbook starts by deleting a production table if an alert fires.
example_out: A runbook that starts with read-only checks, removes the destructive first step, and escalates before any data deletion.

name: slo-error-budget
title: SLO and Error Budget
summary: Draft an SLO from a user journey and explain how the error budget changes release behavior.
example: A team copies a 99.99 SLO from a blog and has no latency metric.
example_out: A draft that refuses the copied target, names the missing metric, and proposes a journey-based indicator.

name: tech-debt-triage
title: Tech Debt Triage
summary: Triage tech debt by the risk and delay it causes, and cut the list to what the team will actually pay down.
example: A team has 60 debt tickets and wants them all in next sprint alongside a launch.
example_out: A triage that keeps the debt tied to launch risk, parks the rest, and makes the capacity trade explicit.

name: technical-design-doc
title: Technical Design Doc
summary: Write a technical design that states the problem, the constraints, the chosen approach, and the rejected alternative.
example: An engineer proposes a new service but has not said what happens when the dependency is down.
example_out: A design doc with the failure behavior, one rejected alternative, and a rollback path.

name: test-strategy
title: Test Strategy
summary: Choose a test strategy for a change that matches risk, instead of demanding every kind of test.
example: A team argues about coverage percent while a refund path has no test.
example_out: A strategy that prioritizes the refund path and treats the coverage number as secondary.

name: threat-model-lite
title: Lightweight Threat Model
summary: Sketch a defensive threat model for a feature: assets, actors, abuses, and controls. No exploit steps.
example: A file-sharing feature has no answer for who can access a link.
example_out: A note that lists unauthorized access as a gap, recommends an access control and audit event, and includes no exploit procedure.

name: assumption-map
title: Assumption Map
summary: List the assumptions that would kill the idea if they are wrong, in the founder's words.
example: The killer assumption is that shop owners will pay $49 a month. They have not asked.
example_out: A map with that sentence as the killer and the test not yet run.

name: beachhead-market
title: Beachhead Market
summary: Pick the first market from the customers they can already reach.
example: They can talk to Airdrie shop owners this month. A draft targets every small business in Canada.
example_out: A beachhead of the shops they can visit, and Canada marked as not now.

name: customer-discovery-sprint
title: Customer Discovery Sprint
summary: Plan a discovery sprint that books real conversations and writes down disconfirming evidence.
example: A sprint plan interviews the founder's family and calls it validation.
example_out: A sprint that recruits people with the problem and requires a disconfirming log.

name: design-partner-pilot
title: Design Partner Pilot
summary: Scope a pilot with the partner, the success test, and the end date.
example: A shop agreed to try exports for 30 days. A draft calls the company validated.
example_out: A pilot with a 30-day end and no validated claim.

name: first-ten-customers
title: First Ten Customers
summary: List the first customers they can name, and the ones that are still wishes.
example: Four shops pay. Six names are on a wish list with no conversation. A deck says ten customers.
example_out: A list of four paying shops, and the six wishes marked as not customers.

name: founder-operating-review
title: Founder Operating Review
summary: Run a weekly founder review of cash, pipeline, and the one bottleneck.
example: A review adds five new ideas while payroll is the unresolved issue.
example_out: A review that keeps payroll as the bottleneck and parks the new ideas.

name: idea-screen
title: Idea Screen
