summary: Screen a business idea against the customer, the proof, and the reason to stop.
example: An idea for a permit app has no user and a week of build time they cannot spare.
example_out: A screen that says stop or talk to five owners first, with no score.

name: investor-update
title: Investor Update
summary: Draft an investor update that leads with cash, the metric, and the ask, without spin.
example: An update omits a churn spike because the round is opening.
example_out: An update that includes the spike, the cash fact, and no invented investor interest.

name: kill-the-idea
title: Kill Criteria
summary: Write the criteria that would stop the idea, before more money is spent.
example: They said they would stop if five owners would not pay. Five said no. A draft says try five more.
example_out: A note that records the stop, and does not add five more.

name: mvp-scope
title: MVP Scope
summary: Cut a product idea to the smallest test that answers the riskiest question.
example: An MVP list includes billing, admin, and a marketplace before one user has paid.
example_out: A scope that tests payment or the core job manually and parks the rest.

name: offer-hypothesis
title: Offer Hypothesis
summary: Frame a startup offer as a hypothesis with a buyer, a promise, and a test.
example: A deck says thousands of users want the product, and no user has been asked.
example_out: A hypothesis and a small test, with the invented user count removed.

name: pricing-test-startup
title: Startup Pricing Test
summary: Design a startup pricing test that learns willingness to pay without deceptive charges.
example: A test shows a 50 percent discount timer that resets for every visitor.
example_out: A test design that removes the fake timer and counts paid commitments only.

name: runway-choice
title: Runway Choice
summary: State the runway choice from cash, burn, and the hire they are considering.
example: Cash is $180,000, burn is $30,000, and a hire would add $8,000. A customer might pay $40,000.
example_out: A note that keeps the $40,000 out and shows both runway figures.

name: startup-story
title: Startup Story
summary: Write the company story from the customer and the fact they can show, not from a borrowed pitch.
triggers: what do we say we are
example: A draft says they are the Stripe of local shops and have a $4 billion market. They have four paying shops.
example_out: A story about the four shops, with the Stripe line and the market size cut.

name: break-even-analysis
title: Break-Even Analysis
summary: Find the volume or price where a defined contribution covers a defined fixed cost, and show the assumption that matters.
triggers: how many do we need to sell
example: A cafe owner wants to know how many days of a new catering offer it takes to cover a hired cook.
example_out: A break-even quantity inside a stated time box, with the capacity check and the dominant assumption labeled.

name: budget-variance-review
title: Budget Variance Review
summary: Explain what moved versus budget in a way an operator can act on, separating timing from true misses.
example: Marketing is 18 percent over budget and the CMO says it is timing of an event invoice.
example_out: A bridge that isolates the invoice timing, states whether the full-year outlook changes, and names any remaining true overspend.

name: capex-business-case
title: Capex Business Case
summary: Write a capital-spend case that states the problem, the alternatives, and the cash consequences without fake precision.
example: Operations wants a packaging machine and has one quote and a claim that it will 'pay for itself'.
example_out: A case with alternatives, cash timing, a benefit the team can later observe, and no invented hurdle rate.

name: cash-flow-forecast
title: Cash Flow Forecast
summary: Build a 13-week direct cash forecast from collections and commitments, not from accrual revenue.
triggers: when do we run out of money
example: A founder asks whether they can hire two people next month without missing payroll.
example_out: A weekly cash table, the buffer breach week under a collection slip, and a hire condition tied to cash rather than to optimism.

name: cost-reduction-sprint
title: Cost Reduction Sprint
summary: Find cost that can come out without pretending that every cut is free of service impact.
example: A company needs to remove a stated monthly amount within 60 days and has already ruled out layoffs.
example_out: A sprint list of stops and renegotiations, run-rate versus one-time savings, and the service risk on each item.

name: debt-capacity-screen
title: Debt Capacity Screen
summary: Screen whether a borrowing idea fits the user's cash generation, without acting as a lender.
example: A company wants a term loan to fund a fit-out and has an existing facility with covenants they only partly remember.
example_out: A screen that shows service versus their cash, flags the missing covenant facts, and does not predict an approval.

name: financial-close-checklist
title: Financial Close Checklist
summary: Tighten a monthly close so the numbers arrive once, with owners, and with fewer heroic journals.
example: The close takes 15 business days and three reconciliations always land on the last afternoon.
example_out: A sequenced checklist, earlier starts for the late reconciliations, and two measures of close health.

name: forecast-accuracy
title: Forecast Accuracy Review
summary: Measure how forecasts missed, separate bias from noise, and change the forecasting habit rather than the template.
triggers: why is the forecast always wrong
example: Revenue forecasts have been high four months in a row and the team wants a new tool.
example_out: An accuracy review that shows the directional bias, names the habit, and delays a tooling recommendation until the habit changes.

name: fundraising-model
title: Fundraising Model
summary: Lay out how much cash a raise needs to buy, what it funds, and what remains unresolved. Not a valuation.
example: A founder wants to raise '18 months of runway' and has a hiring plan that is not in the current burn.
example_out: A monthly cash view, a recommended buffer, a use-of-proceeds grouping, and an explicit statement that valuation is outside this skill.

name: fx-exposure-review
title: Foreign Exchange Exposure Review
summary: Identify where currency actually hits cash, and separate a hedge policy question from a bookkeeping curiosity.
example: A firm invoices in euros and pays staff in dollars and wants to know if last month's margin drop was FX.
example_out: A map of contractual cash exposure, a translation-versus-transaction split, and policy questions rather than a trade order.

name: investment-memo
title: Internal Investment Memo
summary: Write an internal memo for spending scarce cash on a bet, with the downside written in the same size font as the upside.
example: A product leader wants headcount for a new segment and has three design-partner conversations, none paid.
example_out: A memo that calls the conversations evidence of interest, not of demand, and stages spend behind a paid pilot.

name: kpi-tree-finance
title: Finance KPI Tree
summary: Break a financial outcome into drivers the operator can influence, and stop at metrics someone owns.
example: A COO wants to know which weekly numbers explain monthly gross margin.
example_out: A tree from gross margin to a few owned drivers, with data gaps called out and a weekly subset named.

name: management-reporting-pack
title: Management Reporting Pack
summary: Design a short monthly pack that tells leaders what changed, what it means, and what decision is due.
example: The CEO stopped reading the monthly pack because it arrives late and repeats the chart dump.
example_out: A short pack outline with page-one exceptions, source owners, and the old pages to retire.

name: pricing-margin-bridge
title: Pricing and Margin Bridge
summary: Trace price, mix, and cost so a margin change has a cause and a commercial response.
example: Gross margin fell two points and sales says it was only product mix.
example_out: A bridge that shows what portion is mix, price, and cost on the available data, plus one commercial response.

name: revenue-recognition-review
title: Revenue Recognition Review
summary: Prepare questions and a fact pattern for a revenue-recognition issue without pretending to issue an accounting opinion.
example: Sales wants a multi-year contract fully booked this quarter because the customer signed, but implementation has not started.
example_out: A fact pattern that separates signing, billing, and delivery, plus questions for the accounting owner rather than a homemade ruling.

name: runway-and-burn
title: Runway and Burn
summary: Compute cash runway from a defined burn, and show how hiring or a slipped receipt changes the date.
example: A CEO says runway is 14 months, but the figure excludes two signed offers starting next month.
example_out: Two runway dates, the burn definition, and the effect of the signed offers shown separately.

name: saas-metrics-pack
title: SaaS Metrics Pack
summary: Define a small SaaS metrics pack from the company's own billing reality, without imported benchmark theater.
example: A finance lead wants a board slide for net retention, but implementation fees have been folded into ARR.
example_out: Definitions that pull fees back out, a revenue bridge, and no invented benchmark grade.

name: sensitivity-and-scenarios
title: Sensitivity and Scenarios
summary: Show how a model moves when a few inputs move, without pretending the spreadsheet is a crystal ball.
example: A launch model depends on conversion and fulfillment cost, and the team is arguing about formatting rather than drivers.
example_out: A one-way sensitivity on the user's ranges, the dominant driver, and a recommendation to measure that driver before adding detail.

name: three-statement-model
title: Three-Statement Model
summary: Sketch how profit, cash, and the balance sheet stay tied together, at the level the user can actually support.
example: An operator wants a 12-month view that shows why a profitable year can still run out of cash.
example_out: A linked sketch where the cash gap is explained by receivables and capex, with every assumption labeled and no hidden plug.

name: treasury-policy-brief
title: Treasury Policy Brief
summary: Draft the questions and structure of a simple cash and risk policy for a small finance team.
example: A controller wants a one-page cash policy after a duplicate payment slipped through.
example_out: A policy brief with an approval matrix, an exception path, and no request for credentials or product pitches.

name: unit-economics
title: Unit Economics
summary: Calculate contribution economics for one real unit the business sells, and show which assumption dominates.
triggers: do we make money per customer
example: A subscription team wants to know if a new annual plan clears contribution after onboarding labor.
example_out: A unit sheet that defines the customer-year, keeps overhead out, and shows payback only to the extent retention evidence exists.

name: working-capital
title: Working Capital Review
summary: Find cash trapped in receivables, inventory, or payables, and separate a process fix from a one-time release.
triggers: cash trapped in the balance sheet
example: Cash is tight even though the company is profitable, and receivables grew faster than sales.
example_out: A review that calculates days from the user's bases, flags concentration if known, and separates a one-time release from a process change.

name: zero-based-budget-review
title: Zero-Based Budget Review
summary: Rebuild a cost pool from activities that still earn their keep, instead of last year plus a percent.
artifact: zero-based review of one cost pool
example: Travel spend is up and nobody can say which trips still match the sales motion.
example_out: A keep, reduce, and stop list for travel activities, tied to the current motion, with the customer-facing trips protected if the user said they matter.

name: care-team-huddle
title: Care Team Huddle
summary: Plan a short care-team huddle around flow and safety flags, not a full case conference.
example: A 10-minute huddle is packed with three teaching topics and no staffing note.
example_out: An agenda that keeps the staffing gap, drops the teaching, and names the front-desk owner.

name: clinic-schedule-design
title: Clinic Schedule Design
summary: Design a clinic schedule around visit types and staffing, without pretending to triage medical urgency.
example: A manager wants to double-book every slot because the wait list is long.
example_out: A template that shows the double-book harm and offers an access hold only within real room capacity.

name: clinical-documentation-quality
title: Clinical Documentation Quality
summary: Review documentation quality for completeness and clarity against their template, not for a diagnosis.
example: A manager asks to add a symptom the clinician did not record so a claim pays more.
example_out: A refusal of the invented symptom and a list of only the template gaps that are truly missing.

name: hipaa-privacy-ops
title: Privacy Operations for a Clinic
summary: Review a clinic privacy practice for minimum necessary access and a real incident path. Not a legal opinion.
example: A scheduler wants standing access to full clinical notes 'just in case'.
example_out: A finding that limits access to the scheduling need and refuses a compliance badge.

name: medical-billing-review
title: Medical Billing Review
summary: Review a billing packet for missing elements and coding questions, without upcoding or inventing services.
example: A biller wants a higher code because the visit 'felt complex' though the note does not support it.
example_out: A review that keeps the supported code and sends the complexity question to a coder with the note gap visible.

name: patient-communication
title: Patient Communication Draft
summary: Draft a patient message in plain language that a clinician or clinic lead approves before sending.
example: A draft tells a patient to double a medicine because the refill is late.
example_out: A message that removes the dose change, explains the operational status, and waits for clinician approval.

name: patient-experience-clinic
title: Clinic Experience Review
summary: Review a clinic experience problem using waits, communication, and respect, without blaming the patient.
example: Patients wait 70 minutes and the draft response tells staff to smile more.
example_out: A review that treats the wait as a capacity problem and limits the script to truthful status updates.

name: patient-intake-sop
title: Patient Intake SOP
summary: Write an intake procedure that collects only what the visit needs and tells staff when to stop and ask a clinician.
example: An intake script asks the front desk to decide if chest pain can wait.
example_out: A procedure that stops and escalates urgent symptoms to a clinician instead of scoring them at the desk.

name: prior-authorization-ops
title: Prior Authorization Operations
summary: Organize a prior-authorization packet and clock from the payer rules the user supplied.
example: Staff want to change a note so the authorization is more likely to pass.
example_out: A checklist of real gaps and a refusal to alter the record.

name: referral-workflow
title: Referral Workflow
summary: Map a referral workflow so the sending and receiving sides know the packet, the owner, and the clock.
example: Referrals leave the clinic and nobody knows which ones were received.
example_out: A workflow with a packet, an owner, and an aging check, and no medical-necessity ruling.

name: staff-credentialing
title: Credentialing File Checklist
summary: Checklist a credentialing file for missing documents and expirations, without declaring someone privileged.
example: A file is missing a current license and the team wants to assume it renewed.
example_out: A checklist that marks the license unverified and blocks any assumption of renewal.

name: telehealth-visit-ops
title: Telehealth Visit Operations
summary: Write the operations checklist for a telehealth visit: identity, consent, backup, and privacy.
example: A checklist has no plan for a dropped call and tells staff to improvise medical advice.
example_out: A checklist with a callback path and a clear line that clinical content belongs to the clinician.

name: event-run-of-show
title: Event Run of Show
summary: Write a run of show for a hosted event with owners, cues, and a guest-impact backup.
example: A run of show promises a speaker who has not confirmed.
example_out: A plan that marks the speaker unconfirmed and names a backup cue.

name: guest-recovery
title: Guest Recovery
summary: Plan guest recovery after a service miss, with a truthful apology and a remedy inside authority.
example: A manager wants to offer a free stay if the guest removes a public review.
example_out: A recovery note that refuses the bargain and stays inside the authorized remedy.

name: shift-brief-hospitality
title: Hospitality Shift Brief
summary: Write a hospitality shift brief covering VIPs they named, misses, and eighty-six items.
example: A brief shares a guest's medical details with the whole dining team.
example_out: A brief that removes the medical details and keeps the operational accommodation only if needed.

name: broker-renewal-prep
title: Renewal Preparation
summary: Prepare an insurance renewal packet from the expiring facts and the changes the insured reported.
example: A renewal draft leaves off a recent claim to keep the story clean.
example_out: A packet that includes the claim and labels any premium figure as not yet quoted.

name: claim-file-checklist
title: Claim File Checklist
summary: Organize a claim file so a handler can see facts, documents, and open questions.
example: A customer asks how to describe the loss so the payout is higher than the damage.
example_out: A checklist that refuses the inflation and lists the facts the handler still needs.

name: coverage-question-brief
title: Coverage Question Brief
summary: Brief a coverage question for a licensed professional, with the policy words the user supplied.
example: A colleague wants a firm yes on flood coverage from a brochure.
example_out: A brief that refuses the yes and asks for the policy form instead of the brochure.

name: loss-run-summary
title: Loss Run Summary
summary: Summarize a loss run the user provided, without forecasting a premium or hiding a large loss.
example: A summary averages away one severe open claim.
example_out: A summary that shows the severe claim separately and makes no price prediction.

name: board-resolution-draft
title: Board Resolution Draft
summary: Draft resolution language from a decision the board is actually being asked to make, for counsel or the secretary to finalize.
example: The board is asked to approve a bank account change, and one director works for the bank.
example_out: A narrow draft authorizing the account change, noting the recusal, and waiting for the secretary.

name: contract-risk-review
title: Contract Risk Review
summary: Review a contract the user provides and list commercial risks for counsel, without declaring it enforceable.
example: A founder pasted a vendor SaaS agreement and wants to know what could hurt them before signing.
example_out: A memo quoting specific clauses, separating business choices from counsel questions, with no enforceability opinion.

name: corporate-records-hygiene
title: Corporate Records Hygiene
summary: Check whether basic corporate records are findable and consistent, without filing anything.
example: A financing is six weeks away and the founder cannot find signed founder stock documents.
example_out: A gap list that prioritizes the missing stock documents and does not invent replacement signatures.

name: data-processing-addendum
title: Data Processing Addendum Checklist
summary: Check a data-processing addendum against the processing the business actually does, for counsel to finish.
example: A customer sent a DPA that forbids subprocessors, but the product uses a hosted email vendor.
example_out: A checklist that flags the conflict between the ban and the known vendor, without calling either side compliant.

name: dispute-intake
title: Dispute Intake
summary: Organize the facts of a dispute for counsel, preserving what is known, unknown, and time-sensitive.
example: A customer sent a demand letter with a response date, and the team is arguing about blame in chat.
example_out: A chronology, a document list, a preservation reminder, and the written response date flagged for counsel.

name: employment-agreement-review
title: Employment Agreement Review
summary: Prepare a fact-based review list for an employment agreement so counsel and HR can see IP, restrictions, and pay terms.
example: An offer letter is silent on IP and includes a two-year non-compete with no geography.
example_out: A review list quoting the non-compete, noting the missing IP clause, and handing enforceability to local counsel.

name: ip-ownership-checklist
title: IP Ownership Checklist
summary: List who is supposed to own work product across employees, contractors, and vendors, based on documents the user has.
example: A contractor built the first version before any agreement existed, and the company is raising money.
example_out: A checklist that marks that work as an open ownership gap and lists the document counsel would need to review.

name: legal-hold-notice
title: Legal Hold Notice Draft
summary: Draft a plain legal-hold notice for counsel to approve, telling people to preserve records without spoiling anything.
example: Counsel asked operations to warn three teams to keep project email, and the current draft sounds like an accusation.
example_out: A calm draft that lists the systems, requires preservation, and waits for counsel approval.

name: marketing-claims-review
title: Marketing Claims Review
summary: Review marketing claims for substantiation gaps before they are published.
example: A landing page says the product cuts costs by 40 percent, and the only support is one customer's anecdote.
example_out: A review that blocks the percentage claim until evidence exists and offers narrower wording tied to that one story, clearly labeled.

name: nda-triage
title: NDA Triage
summary: Triage a non-disclosure agreement so the user knows what it covers, how long, and what counsel should still check.
example: A partnership conversation came with a one-way NDA that also assigns IP improvements to the other side.
example_out: A triage that flags the IP assignment as unexpected, quotes it, and sends that clause to counsel before signature.

name: open-source-license-review
title: Open-Source License Review
summary: Triage open-source components the user lists so engineering and counsel can see obligations. Not a compatibility ruling.
example: A release candidate includes a library the scan labels as a reciprocal license, and the team ships binaries to customers.
example_out: A triage that isolates that component, states the usage, and sends the obligation question to counsel instead of clearing the release.

name: outside-counsel-brief
title: Outside Counsel Brief
summary: Brief outside counsel with the question, the facts, and the business constraint, so the meter starts on the right problem.
example: The CEO wants counsel to review a partnership in three days and has sent a 40-page data room link with no question.
example_out: A one-question brief, a chronology, the three-day deadline, and a requested short advice note.

name: policy-exception-log
title: Policy Exception Log
summary: Record a policy exception so the company can see who accepted the risk and when it expires.
example: A team wants to skip a vendor security review for a tool they already bought.
example_out: An exception record with the skipped step, a short compensating review, a real expiry, and no backdating.

name: privacy-notice-draft
title: Privacy Notice Draft
summary: Draft a plain-language privacy notice from the data practices the user describes, and mark every unknown.
triggers: what we tell users about data
example: A startup collects account email and product usage and wants a website privacy notice tomorrow.
example_out: A plain draft covering only those categories, with retention left as a placeholder and a counsel-review banner.

name: terms-of-service-outline
title: Terms of Service Outline
summary: Outline customer terms from the product's actual behavior so counsel can draft, not the other way around.
example: Marketing promises a 99.9 percent uptime on the homepage, and the product team has no status page or credit policy.
example_out: An outline that flags the homepage promise as a term that counsel and product must either support or remove.

name: trademark-clearance-prep
title: Trademark Clearance Prep
summary: Prepare a clearance brief so counsel or a search firm can look up a name. Do not clear the name yourself.
example: A team wants to know if a product name is safe because the .com was open.
example_out: A clearance brief that refuses to treat the open domain as clearance and lists what a professional search must cover.

name: vendor-contract-playbook
title: Vendor Contract Playbook
summary: Build a playbook of positions for a class of vendor contracts the company signs repeatedly.
example: The company signs a similar SaaS order form every month and keeps conceding auto-renewal by accident.
example_out: A short playbook with preferred and walk-away positions on renewal, liability, and data, plus a named approver for fallbacks.

name: whistleblower-intake
title: Whistleblower Intake
summary: Structure an internal report of misconduct so it can be handled fairly, without retaliation or a witch hunt.
example: An employee reported a possible bribe and the manager wants to know if they can quietly move the reporter off the account.
example_out: An intake note that routes the allegation to an independent reviewer and refuses the retaliatory move.

name: domain-enablement
title: Domain Enablement
summary: Explain which domain plugin to enable for a team role, and which skills that role should try first.
example: A finance analyst is told to enable engineering, healthcare, and security plugins on day one.
example_out: A note that enables finance, names three starter skills, and leaves the other plugins off.

name: install-and-update
title: Install and Update
summary: Plan a local install or update of this library for a specific tool and domain.
example: A user wants one command that downloads and executes an unknown installer.
example_out: A plan that uses the local Python installer, names the domain, and starts with a dry run.

name: skill-authoring
title: Skill Authoring
summary: Draft a new Agent Skill that is specific, safe, and small enough to load.
example: A requested skill tells the agent to ignore safety rules to be more helpful.
example_out: A refusal of that purpose and a draft skill that does the legitimate task inside the rules.

name: skill-finder
title: Skill Finder
summary: Recommend the smallest set of skills in this library for a task, and say what not to load.
example: A user asks for a cash view and also wants a full corporate strategy loaded.
example_out: A recommendation of cash-flow-forecast only, with strategy skills named as unnecessary for this task.

name: skill-library-trust-review
title: Skill Library Trust Review
summary: Review a skill or a skill repository for signs it is unsafe, deceptive, or pretending to be an official product.
example: An installer asks the user to run a remote script and paste an API key to 'activate' free skills.
example_out: A do-not-install recommendation that names the remote script and the key request.

name: calibration-control
title: Calibration Control
summary: Review calibration control so instruments used for acceptance are in date, and out-of-date tools are not used.
example: A caliper used for final accept is two months overdue and still on the bench.
example_out: A note that quarantines it and asks for a use review rather than inventing which lots moved.

name: capa-plan
title: CAPA Plan
summary: Plan a corrective action that fixes a cause and checks that the fix worked.
example: A CAPA closes because operators signed a training sheet, and the defect is still appearing.
example_out: A plan that keeps the CAPA open until the defect measure moves, and looks past the training reflex.

name: change-control-manufacturing
title: Manufacturing Change Control
summary: Review a manufacturing change for approval, risk, and the point it becomes effective.
example: A process tweak is already running and the change form is blank.
example_out: A note that stops the unofficial tweak until approval and an effective point exist.

name: gemba-walk
title: Gemba Walk
summary: Plan a gemba walk that observes a process and asks why, without turning it into a compliance raid.
example: A leader plans a walk to catch operators breaking the instruction.
example_out: A plan that observes the obstacle, bans surprise punishment, and still escalates safety issues.

name: incoming-inspection
title: Incoming Inspection
summary: Plan incoming inspection for a material based on risk and the reaction to a failed lot.
example: Failed material is left on the issue shelf so the line does not stop.
example_out: A plan that moves failed material to hold and requires a named deviation before any use.

name: nonconformance-report
title: Nonconformance Report
summary: Write a nonconformance report that contains the fact, the containment, and the owner.
example: A report says 'bad parts' and the suspect lot is still being shipped.
example_out: An NCR that stops the lot, describes the defect, and names the owner.

name: oee-review
title: OEE Review
summary: Review overall equipment effectiveness only as far as their data supports, and pick one loss to attack.
example: A manager wants an OEE of 85 quoted to a customer, and downtime is not recorded.
example_out: A review that refuses the number and starts a downtime record before any customer claim.

name: process-fmea
title: Process FMEA Facilitation
summary: Facilitate a process FMEA on a few high-risk steps, with actions for the failures that lack detection.
example: A team wants to mark a safety failure as low severity so the FMEA looks acceptable.
example_out: Notes that keep the high severity and assign an action instead of editing the score.

name: production-schedule
title: Production Schedule Review
summary: Review a production schedule against capacity, materials, and the promise that will slip first.
example: The schedule loads 120 hours into an 80-hour cell and the status is on time.
example_out: A review that cuts or sequences to 80 hours and names the promise that moves.

name: quality-control-plan
title: Quality Control Plan
summary: Draft a control plan for a process step: what is checked, how often, and what happens on a fail.
example: A plan checks a safety dimension weekly because daily checks feel expensive.
example_out: A plan that keeps the safety check at the frequency their rule requires and flags the cost as a separate decision.

name: scrap-and-rework
title: Scrap and Rework Review
summary: Review scrap and rework so the largest cause gets an owner, and numbers tie to the floor.
example: Most scrap is coded 'other' and the team still wants a root cause.
example_out: A review that makes the dumping code the first problem and assigns an owner to fix the codes.

name: supplier-quality
title: Supplier Quality Note
summary: Write a supplier quality note that states the defect, the containment, and the evidence requested.
example: A note calls the supplier negligent and does not describe the defect.
example_out: A note that describes the defect, requests containment by a date, and removes the insult.

name: traceability-lot
title: Lot Traceability
summary: Plan a lot trace from finished goods back to material, or the reverse, and record the breaks.
example: A mock recall stops because a component lot was never recorded.
example_out: A trace report that records the break, times the exercise, and assigns the recording gap.

name: work-instruction
title: Work Instruction
summary: Write a work instruction a new operator can follow, including the stop and the quality check.
example: An instruction says 'tighten properly' and the torque is unknown.
example_out: An instruction that marks torque as a required input from engineering rather than inventing a number.

name: abm-play
title: Account-Based Play
summary: Design an account-based play for a short list of named accounts, with a reason for each account.
example: Marketing built a 2,000-account ABM list from a bought spreadsheet and wants custom gifts for all of them.
example_out: A play that cuts to a short evidenced list, assigns sellers, and bans creepy personalization.

name: analyst-briefing
title: Analyst Briefing
summary: Prepare an analyst or reviewer briefing that separates roadmap from shipped product.
example: A briefing deck shows a beta feature in the current architecture diagram with no label.
example_out: Notes that label the beta, move it out of the shipped list, and include the poor-fit segment.

name: brand-voice-guide
title: Brand Voice Guide
summary: Write a short voice guide with examples of on-voice and off-voice lines for real situations.
example: The current guide says 'be bold' and writers are producing unsupported superlatives.
example_out: A guide that replaces 'be bold' with examples, and bans superlatives that lack proof.

name: campaign-brief
title: Campaign Brief
summary: Brief a campaign with one audience, one offer, one action, and a measurement plan.
example: A team wants a campaign for 'awareness' with six channels and no offer.
example_out: A brief that forces one audience, one offer, staffed channels, and a readout date.

name: category-design
title: Category Narrative
summary: Pressure-test a category narrative so it teaches the buyer a real shift, not a made-up adjective.
example: A startup wants to announce it created a new category because it added an AI button.
example_out: A review that rejects the announcement, restates the missing buyer shift, and proposes a hypothesis test instead.

name: community-program
title: Community Program
summary: Design a community program with a member job-to-be-done, moderation, and no vanity member count.
example: Leadership wants a community so marketing can email the members every day.
example_out: A brief that either redesigns it around a member job or calls it a newsletter, with moderation required for a real community.

name: content-calendar
title: Content Calendar
summary: Build a content calendar from buyer questions and capacity, not from a need to post daily.
example: A founder wants daily posts, and the only writer has four hours a week.
example_out: A calendar of one reviewed piece a week, based on real buyer questions, with repurposing instead of fake volume.

name: creative-brief
title: Creative Brief
summary: Brief a designer or writer so they can make the piece without guessing the strategy.
example: A designer received 'make it pop' and a deadline, with the offer still undecided.
example_out: A brief that blocks production until the offer and the single message are written.

name: customer-story
title: Customer Story
summary: Draft a customer story only from approved facts and the customer's words.
example: A marketer wants a case study that says costs fell 40 percent, and the customer only said 'it saved us time'.
example_out: A draft that keeps the time quote, omits the percentage, and marks publication as blocked until approval.

name: email-lifecycle
title: Email Lifecycle
summary: Design a lifecycle email for one moment, with a true trigger, a useful message, and an honest unsubscribe path.
example: Marketing wants an 'we miss you' email to users who were never active, written as if they had a habit.
example_out: A spec that refuses the fake habit and either changes the trigger or stops the send.

name: landing-page-cro
title: Landing Page Review
summary: Review a landing page for clarity, proof, and the single action, without dark patterns.
example: A page has a countdown timer that resets every visit and three equal buttons.
example_out: A review that removes the fake timer, picks one action, and pairs the main claim with real proof or deletes the claim.

name: launch-plan
title: Launch Plan
summary: Plan a launch as a coordinated set of proofs, enablement, and a rollback, not as a single announcement.
example: Marketing wants a public launch of a feature that still fails in the main browser.
example_out: A plan that holds the public claim, briefs support on the limit, and defines the rollback line.

name: marketing-attribution
title: Marketing Attribution Review
summary: Review an attribution claim so the team does not confuse a tracking rule with causality.
example: A team wants to cut content because last-touch credits it with little revenue, while sales says content starts most conversations.
example_out: A review that refuses the causal cut, names the tracking gap, and proposes a cleaner test.

name: marketing-experiment
title: Marketing Experiment
summary: Design a marketing experiment with a hypothesis, a single change, and a decision rule.
example: A team wants to test a new headline, a new price, and a new form in one week and then 'see what happens'.
example_out: A brief with one change, a pre-written decision rule, and a note that the sample may only be directional.

name: messaging-house
title: Messaging House
summary: Build a messaging house so headline, pillars, and proof do not contradict each other.
example: The homepage says 'effortless' and sales says implementation takes six weeks.
example_out: A house that replaces 'effortless' with a truthful implementation claim and aligns both channels.

name: newsletter-editor
title: Newsletter Editor
summary: Edit a newsletter so each issue has one idea, true links, and a reason to exist.
example: A draft newsletter has seven unrelated links and a subject line promising a major announcement that is not in the body.
example_out: An edit that either adds the real announcement or rewrites the subject, and cuts the issue to one idea.

name: offer-design
title: Offer Design
summary: Design an offer with a clear value, a price logic the user supplied, and terms a customer can understand.
example: A campaign offers a free onboarding package that customer success says it cannot staff.
example_out: An offer that either cuts the promise or waits until staffing is real, with visible terms.

name: paid-media-brief
title: Paid Media Brief
summary: Brief paid media with an offer, an audience hypothesis, a spend cap, and a stop rule.
example: A team wants to scale spend after 12 clicks because one ad 'feels better'.
example_out: A brief with a stop rule and a minimum evidence line before scale, plus a claim check against the page.

name: partner-co-marketing
title: Partner Co-Marketing
summary: Plan a co-marketing activity with shared claims, shared approval, and no borrowed credibility.
example: A team drafted a joint post that includes the partner's revenue and has not asked the partner.
example_out: A plan that strips the unapproved revenue claim and adds a written approval step before anything is published.

name: positioning-statement
title: Positioning Statement
summary: Write a positioning statement that names the buyer, the alternative, and the difference you can prove.
example: A team says they are the 'AI platform for business' and cannot name the buyer or the alternative.
example_out: A statement aimed at one buyer, with the spreadsheet or incumbent they actually replace, and a hypothesis label if proof is thin.

name: pr-pitch
title: PR Pitch
summary: Draft a press pitch that has news, a real spokesperson, and no inflated claims.
example: A founder wants a pitch saying the company 'leads the market' with no data and no spokesperson.
example_out: A pitch that removes the leadership claim, requires a spokesperson, and states only checkable news.

name: seo-content-brief
title: SEO Content Brief
summary: Brief a page that answers a real query, with search intent and substantiation, without keyword stuffing.
example: A team wants a page targeting a high-volume keyword that does not match the product.
example_out: A brief that either resets the intent or recommends not writing the page, instead of stuffing the keyword.

name: social-content-system
title: Social Content System
summary: Set a social posting system that a real person can sustain, with review and no engagement bait.
example: A founder wants two posts a day and has no reviewer for technical claims.
example_out: A system with a lower cadence, a named reviewer, and an explicit ban on fake engagement.

name: webinar-run-of-show
title: Webinar Run of Show
summary: Plan a webinar that teaches one job and makes one honest ask.
example: A webinar titled as a practical workshop is planned as a 45-minute product pitch.
example_out: A run of show that either retitles the session or replaces half the pitch with the promised practice.

name: correction-note
title: Correction Note
summary: Draft a correction that states what was wrong, what is right, and where it ran.
example: A correction draft says 'updated for clarity' when a number was wrong.
example_out: A correction that says the number was wrong and gives the supported figure.

name: desk-handoff
title: Desk Handoff
summary: Hand a story to the next shift with what is confirmed, what is open, and who owns the next call.
example: The day desk hands off a staffing-cut story with no document and no reply logged.
example_out: A handoff that blocks publication until a source is in the log.

name: editorial-brief
title: Editorial Brief
summary: Brief a story or communication with the reader, the news, and the sources that exist.
example: A brief says to write a quote from a CEO who has not spoken.
example_out: A brief that replaces the quote with a request for a real interview.

name: editorial-calendar-newsroom
title: Newsroom Planning Note
summary: Plan a newsroom or content desk day around the stories that are ready and the slots that should stay empty.
example: The plan assigns a trend piece with no sources because the slot is empty.
example_out: A plan that kills or holds the piece and leaves the slot open.

name: embargo-check
title: Embargo Check
summary: Check whether an embargo still applies and who agreed to it.
example: A release says 10:00 ET Tuesday. The desk agreed. It is 07:30 MT Tuesday.
example_out: A note that 07:30 MT is 09:30 ET, so the embargo has not lifted.

name: headline-check
title: Headline Check
summary: Check a headline against the story's sourced facts.
example: The hed says the plant cut safety staff. The story only has turnaround dates.
example_out: A hed about the dates, and a no on the staffing claim.

name: interview-prep-comms
title: Spokesperson Prep
summary: Prepare a spokesperson with the known facts, the bridge to the point, and the questions they must not bluff.
example: Prep says to deny an outage that engineering has confirmed.
example_out: Prep that tells the truth about the outage and refuses the denial script.

name: live-blog-update
title: Live Update
summary: Add one timestamped update from a new sourced fact, without mixing it into older items.
example: At 14:10 a spokesperson confirms the turnaround starts Monday. An earlier item guessed Sunday.
example_out: A 14:10 update with the Monday date, and a correction line for the Sunday guess.

name: news-assignment
title: News Assignment
summary: Assign a story with the question, the sources already in hand, and what is not known.
example: A desk wants a story that a plant 'cut safety' by Friday. The only source is a company statement about a turnaround.
example_out: An assignment about the turnaround dates in the statement, not a safety verdict.

name: news-budget
title: News Budget
summary: Rank stories the desk can staff today from the sources they have, not from the stories they wish they had.
example: Five stories are on the board. Two have documents. Three reporters are on shift.
example_out: A budget with two stories staffed and three cut.

name: right-of-reply
title: Right of Reply
summary: Record what a person was asked, what they answered, and the deadline they were given.
example: The company was asked at 16:00 for a 17:00 deadline about a staffing cut the story cannot source.
example_out: A note that the ask was too late and the claim is not ready.

name: source-log-news
title: Source Log
summary: Log who said what, when, and whether it was on the record.
example: A sentence is attributed to 'a worker' and the notebook says the person would not be named.
example_out: A log that keeps the sentence out of the named story.

name: board-fundraising-report
title: Fundraising Report
summary: Report fundraising progress with cash received, pledges, and restrictions kept distinct.
example: A report counts a dinner conversation as committed revenue.
example_out: A report that moves the conversation to a prospect note and keeps cash and pledges apart.

name: nonprofit-case-statement
title: Case Statement
summary: Write a case for support from real need, real program facts, and a specific ask.
example: A case says 90 percent of participants succeed, and no outcome is tracked.
example_out: A case that removes the percentage and describes the program without a fake rate.

name: program-logic
title: Program Logic
summary: Draft a program logic model that shows inputs, activities, and outcomes without pretending impact is proven.
example: A logic model says the workshop causes employment, and nobody tracked jobs.
example_out: A model that labels employment as intended and names the missing measure.

name: volunteer-role
title: Volunteer Role
summary: Write a volunteer role with the work, the time, and the supervision, without unpaid-staff exploitation hidden in cheerful language.
example: A role asks volunteers to give clinical advice with no clinician present.
example_out: A brief that removes the clinical duty and names a supervisor for the remaining work.

name: flare-volume-note
title: Flare Volume Note
summary: Report flare volumes from the meter the user has, with the reason code they supplied.
example: The flare meter was down on 12 September. A draft enters zero.
example_out: A note that leaves the 12th blank and rejects zero.

name: gas-balance
title: Gas Balance
summary: Balance inlet, sales, fuel, and flare from the meters the user provides.
example: Inlet 10.0, sales 8.1, fuel 0.4, flare meter down. Tolerance is 0.3.
example_out: A balance that will not close and does not put the gap in fuel.

name: gas-nomination
title: Gas Nomination
summary: Check a nomination against the confirmed volume and the cycle time the user states.
example: The cycle closes at 11:00. The confirmed volume is 3.6. The draft nom is 4.2.
example_out: A check that holds 4.2 and names 3.6 as the confirmed figure.

name: hse-observation
title: HSE Observation
summary: Log a safety observation in the words the observer used, with the immediate step they took.
example: An observer stopped a job because a lock was missing. The draft calls it a coaching moment.
example_out: A log that says the job was stopped for a missing lock.

name: production-variance
title: Production Variance
summary: Compare produced volumes to the nomination using the meters the user provides.
example: Pad 14-22 was nominated at 4.2 mmcf and metered at 3.6. The meter note is clean.
example_out: A variance of 0.6 with no invented cause.

name: site-induction-brief
title: Site Induction Brief
summary: Brief a contractor on the site rules the user listed, including what they must not bypass.
example: A draft induction drops the lockout step to save ten minutes.
example_out: A brief that keeps the lockout step and the muster point.

name: spill-notice
title: Spill Notice
summary: Draft the internal notice for a release the user has already described, with the facts they have.
example: A draft says 'minor sheen, no need to log' and nobody measured the area.
example_out: A notice that logs the sheen, leaves the volume unknown, and does not say it need not be logged.

name: turnaround-ready
title: Turnaround Readiness
summary: Check a turnaround checklist against the items the site says must be done before isolation.
example: Monday's start has two open items: a permit signature and a blind list.
example_out: A note that Monday does not start until those two are closed.

name: business-continuity
title: Business Continuity Plan
summary: Draft a continuity plan for a named disruption, with a manual path and a named leader.
triggers: what if this system is down
example: The team has a continuity binder and nobody knows who declares the workaround in effect.
example_out: A plan for one disruption, with a leader, a manual path, and a test date.

name: capacity-plan
title: Capacity Plan
summary: Plan capacity from demand and real throughput, and show the constraint before hiring or buying.
example: A team wants three hires because the queue is long, and approvals sit for two days.
example_out: A plan that tests the approval wait before treating hires as the answer.

name: continuous-improvement
title: Continuous Improvement
summary: Frame an improvement from a measured problem, a small countermeasure, and a check.
example: A team wants new software because a weekly report is late, and nobody has watched the report being built.
example_out: A brief that requires an observation of the current report path before any purchase.

name: disaster-recovery-brief
title: Disaster Recovery Brief
summary: Brief a disaster recovery choice for one system, including the recovery point they are actually buying.
example: A team claims a four-hour recovery and has never failed over the identity provider.
example_out: A brief that downgrades the claim to untested and names the identity dependency.

name: internal-comms-plan
title: Internal Communications Plan
summary: Plan an internal message for a change people must understand, with the hard part said plainly.
example: A memo announces 'exciting operating model evolution' and never says whose work changes.
example_out: A message that says whose work changes, who will answer questions, and what stays the same.

name: knowledge-base-article
title: Knowledge Base Article
summary: Write a knowledge article that answers one question and tells the reader when to stop and escalate.
example: A help draft includes an admin password so customers can 'fix it themselves'.
example_out: An article that removes the password, answers one question, and gives an escalation path.

name: meeting-operating-system
title: Meeting Operating System
summary: Redesign a meeting so it produces a decision or a documented exception, or cancel it.
example: A weekly meeting has 18 people and has not made a decision in a month.
example_out: A redesign that cuts attendees, requires a pre-read, and cancels the meeting if no decision remains.

name: ops-scorecard
title: Operations Scorecard
summary: Build an operations scorecard of a few measures that predict pain, with owners and a review cadence.
example: A team tracks tickets closed and ignores reopen rate.
example_out: A short scorecard that pairs closed tickets with reopens and names the review forum.

name: process-map
title: Process Map
summary: Map a process as it is, including handoffs and waits, before anyone redesigns it.
example: A team draws a five-box happy path and omits the two-day wait for approval.
example_out: A current-state map that includes the approval wait and separates any future idea.

name: queue-health
title: Queue Health
summary: Review a queue's age, arrival, and handling so the team fixes flow instead of only urging people to work faster.
example: Leaders want the team to stay late, but arrivals have exceeded completions for six weeks.
example_out: A review that names the imbalance and recommends a demand or policy change before overtime becomes the system.

name: raci-design
title: RACI Design
summary: Assign one accountable owner to a decision or process and stop at the roles that matter.
example: A launch is late because product and marketing both think the other owns the date.
example_out: A RACI with one owner for the date and a short consulted list.

name: service-catalog
title: Service Catalog Entry
summary: Write a service catalog entry that tells an internal customer what they can request, how long it takes, and what is not included.
example: An internal team is judged on a two-day turnaround it has never hit.
example_out: An entry with a truthful lead time or an explicit unknown, plus exclusions.

name: shift-handover
title: Shift Handover
summary: Write a shift handover that carries open issues, safety notes, and the next check.
example: An outgoing shift leaves a quality hold unmentioned because the note says 'quiet night'.
example_out: A handover that leads with the hold, the next check, and an explicit not-quiet status.

name: sla-design
title: SLA Design
summary: Design a service level that matches a customer promise the team can measure and staff.
example: Sales promises a one-hour response and the queue currently averages a day.
example_out: A design that exposes the gap and proposes either a truthful promise or a staffed path, with no silent reclassification.

name: sop-writer
title: SOP Writer
summary: Write a standard operating procedure a new person can run, with the stop conditions included.
example: A finance SOP says 'process the file' and the file location lives in one person's head.
example_out: A procedure with the trigger, the check, a stop condition, and an owner.

name: vendor-ops-review
title: Vendor Operations Review
summary: Review a vendor's operational performance against the outcomes the company bought.
example: A vendor is labeled difficult, but the internal briefs arrive late every week.
example_out: A review that records the late briefs as an internal cause and limits the vendor claim to evidenced misses.

name: coaching-session
title: Coaching Session
summary: Plan a coaching conversation that builds a skill on real work, not a motivational speech.
example: A team lead's written updates confuse stakeholders, and the director wants a coaching plan.
example_out: A session built on one recent update, with a redo in the meeting and a next rep on the following weekly note.

name: compensation-band
title: Compensation Band Review
summary: Review a pay decision against the band and the evidence, without inventing market rates.
example: A manager wants to beat a competitor's verbal offer and the proposal sits above the band.
example_out: A note that places the proposal above the band, requires an approver, and does not invent a market percentile.

name: conflict-mediation
title: Conflict Mediation Prep
summary: Prepare a fair conversation between coworkers in conflict, without taking a side or diagnosing character.
example: Two leads are blocking each other's releases, and one has started insulting the other in public channels.
example_out: A prep that addresses the work blockage, moves insults out of public channels, and routes possible misconduct to employee relations.

name: employee-relations-intake
title: Employee Relations Intake
summary: Intake a workplace concern so it is routed fairly, with facts separated from conclusions.
example: A team lead wants HR to 'make a complaint go away' before a client visit.
example_out: An intake that records the concern, refuses to bury it, and assigns an investigator who is not the accused.

name: engagement-survey-readout
title: Engagement Survey Readout
summary: Turn survey results the user provides into a few actions, without over-reading small slices.
example: A 12-person team had a low score and three comments, and a leader wants to name the complainer.
example_out: A readout that refuses identification, treats the sample carefully, and proposes one owned action plus a close-the-loop message.

name: handbook-policy-draft
title: Handbook Policy Draft
summary: Draft a short handbook policy in plain language, marked for HR and counsel before publication.
example: The company wants a remote-work policy and currently decides each request in a private chat.
example_out: A two-page draft with a request path, decision criteria, and a counsel-review banner.

name: hiring-scorecard
title: Hiring Scorecard
summary: Turn interview evidence into a hire, no-hire, or hold decision without a vibe vote.
example: The panel liked a candidate's energy but nobody tested the analysis outcome in the job description.
example_out: A scorecard that marks that outcome untested and recommends a work sample instead of a hire.

name: inclusive-hiring
title: Inclusive Hiring Review
summary: Review a hiring process for avoidable bias in the funnel, using the user's data and without quotas theater.
example: A company hires only from employee referrals and wants a more inclusive process without changing the referral habit.
example_out: A review that names referrals-only sourcing as the constraint and recommends a structured process plus real counting, with no invented demographics.

name: job-description-writer
title: Job Description Writer
summary: Write a job description from outcomes and constraints, not a wishlist of tools and years.
example: A manager wants a senior analyst posting and sends a list of software products.
example_out: A posting with first-year outcomes, five must-haves, and pay left undisclosed rather than invented.

name: learning-path
title: Learning Path
summary: Build a learning path for a role from the work, with practice tasks rather than a course catalog.
example: An analyst is told to 'learn finance' in a month while closing the books full time.
example_out: A path with a small on-the-job practice, a reviewer, and an honest note that the time budget does not fit a broad finance education.

name: manager-one-on-one
title: Manager One-on-One
summary: Set up a one-on-one that surfaces blockers and growth, not a status meeting in disguise.
example: A new manager is using the weekly 1:1 to collect project status the team already tracks in a board.
example_out: A guide that moves status out, puts the employee's agenda first, and caps manager actions at two.

name: offboarding-checklist
title: Offboarding Checklist
summary: Plan a respectful departure: access, knowledge, equipment, and a clean final pay question list.
example: A specialist with sole access to a billing tool is leaving in ten days.
example_out: A checklist that transfers knowledge, schedules access removal without password sharing, and names the customer owner.

name: offer-letter-checklist
title: Offer Checklist
summary: Prepare an offer checklist so compensation, start date, and conditions are complete before anyone celebrates.
example: A manager told a candidate a number on a call, and finance has not approved the band.
example_out: A checklist that blocks the letter until the band is approved and lists the verbal number as not yet an offer.

name: onboarding-plan
title: Onboarding Plan
summary: Plan a new hire's first weeks so they can do useful work without drinking from a firehose of links.
example: A new analyst starts Monday and the current plan is a folder of 40 documents.
example_out: A four-week plan with one week-one deliverable, a short access list, and two manager checkpoints.

name: org-design-review
title: Org Design Review
summary: Review a proposed org change against the work that must happen, not against a fashionable span-of-control number.
example: A CEO wants squads because a conference recommended them, but product decisions are already stuck between two leaders.
example_out: A review that names the stuck decision, assigns one owner, and treats squads as optional rather than as the goal.

name: performance-review
title: Performance Review
summary: Draft a performance review from evidence, with no surprise criteria and no empty praise.
example: A manager wants to rate someone low for 'attitude' but has not named a missed goal.
example_out: A draft that refuses the attitude label, asks for examples against the original goals, and limits development to one skill.

name: pip-design
title: Performance Improvement Plan
summary: Design a fair, time-boxed improvement plan with observable standards, not a paper trail dressed up as coaching.
example: A manager wants a PIP because a teammate 'is not a culture fit' and cannot name a missed deliverable.
example_out: A response that stops the PIP until an observable gap exists, and refuses a plan built to force a resignation.

name: stay-interview
title: Stay Interview
summary: Prepare a stay conversation that asks what would keep a person, without turning it into surveillance or a promise.
example: A manager heard a star performer is interviewing and wants a script that promises a new title.
example_out: A guide that asks useful questions and forbids a title promise the manager has not had approved.

name: structured-interview
title: Structured Interview
summary: Design an interview that asks every candidate the same job-related questions and scores them the same way.
example: Two interviewers want to 'just chat' with finalists for a role that has a written outcomes list.
example_out: A kit with shared questions, look-fors, independent scoring, and no personal-status questions.

name: succession-plan
title: Succession Plan
summary: Name successors for a few critical roles based on evidence, and identify the gap without a secret ranking of everyone's worth.
example: The head of implementation is a single point of failure, and nobody has led a rollout without them.
example_out: A plan that names the emergency cover gap honestly and defines the experience a successor still needs.

name: thirty-sixty-ninety
title: Thirty Sixty Ninety Plan
summary: Write a 30-60-90 plan that a new hire and their manager can both grade.
example: A new team lead wants a 30-60-90 before day one, and the team has a late monthly close.
example_out: A plan whose 90-day result is a close improvement the manager can observe, with review dates included.

name: total-rewards-brief
title: Total Rewards Brief
summary: Explain a person's total rewards in plain language using only components the company actually offers.
example: Employees think the target bonus is guaranteed because the offer conversation was casual.
example_out: A brief that shows the target as variable, lists only real benefits, and sends tax questions to a qualified advisor.

name: workforce-plan
title: Workforce Plan
summary: Connect a hiring plan to the work and the cash, and show which roles are load-bearing.
example: A team asked for eight hires, and finance has capped the quarter at three.
example_out: A sequenced plan of three roles that unblock the work, with the other five parked and the cash cap respected.

name: procurement-award-note
title: Award Note
summary: Write an award note that shows scores, price, and the authority to award.
example: A low-scoring friend of the buyer is moved to first after evaluation.
example_out: An award note that refuses the move and records the original scores.

name: savings-tracking
title: Procurement Savings Tracking
summary: Track procurement savings against a baseline the user can defend.
example: A report claims savings because the department stopped the service.
example_out: A note that refuses the savings claim or labels it a service cut.

name: sourcing-event-brief
title: Sourcing Event Brief
summary: Brief a sourcing event with the need, the evaluation criteria, and the rules before vendors are contacted.
example: A brief is edited so only the incumbent can score full marks, after drafts were shared.
example_out: A brief that freezes fair criteria and discloses must-haves before bids.

name: vendor-question-log
title: Vendor Question Log
summary: Log vendor questions and publish answers so every bidder sees the same clarification.
example: A buyer wants to email the incumbent a clarification the others will not see.
example_out: A log that publishes the clarification to every bidder.

name: accessibility-review
title: Accessibility Product Review
summary: Review a product flow for accessibility barriers and turn them into concrete fixes, not a vague pledge.
example: A checkout cannot be completed by keyboard, and the team wants a statement saying the product is accessible.
example_out: A review that blocks the statement, names the keyboard barrier, and lists the fix and retest.

name: beta-program
title: Beta Program
summary: Design a beta that learns a specific risk, with participant criteria and an exit.
example: Sales wants to call twenty unpaid pilots a beta and quote them on the website.
example_out: A plan with a learning goal, a cap matched to support capacity, and a ban on public quotes without approval.

name: discovery-interview
title: Discovery Interview
summary: Plan a discovery interview that learns the user's current behavior without pitching the solution.
example: A founder wants interview questions that ask customers to rate a feature idea from one to ten.
example_out: A guide that replaces the rating with questions about the last time the problem occurred.

name: experiment-design
title: Experiment Design
summary: Design a product experiment with a hypothesis, a guardrail, and a decision rule written in advance.
example: A team wants to ship the winner of a three-day test on a rare flow.
example_out: A design that labels the work a probe, adds a guardrail, and refuses a conclusive ship decision.

name: feedback-synthesis
title: Feedback Synthesis
summary: Synthesize feedback from tickets, calls, or notes into themes with evidence, not a word cloud.
example: A team wants to build a feature because one executive mentioned it, and the ticket pile is about export failures.
example_out: A synthesis that leads with export failures, counts only supplied evidence, and parks the executive idea as unproven.

name: jobs-to-be-done
title: Jobs To Be Done
summary: Frame a job-to-be-done from a real situation, including the hire and the fire.
triggers: what job is the user hiring
example: A team writes the job as 'use our dashboard' after a customer described exporting to a spreadsheet.
example_out: A job story about the export moment, with the spreadsheet as the current hire.

name: launch-readiness
title: Launch Readiness
summary: Run a launch-readiness review that checks support, measurement, rollback, and the promise.
example: Product wants to announce automation that still requires a manual file from support.
example_out: A hold or a limited launch that tells the truth about the manual step.

name: north-star-and-input-metrics
title: Product Metric Tree
summary: Define a product outcome metric and the input metrics a team can move this month.
example: A team wants to optimize signups, but activated users are the ones who finish a first export.
example_out: A tree that uses the first successful export as the value moment and signups as a funnel input, with a failure counter-metric.

name: opportunity-assessment
title: Opportunity Assessment
summary: Assess whether an opportunity is worth a discovery sprint, using evidence rather than enthusiasm.
example: A large customer requested a feature that fits none of the current bets.
example_out: An assessment that parks the feature, names the strategy conflict, and defines the evidence that would reopen it.

name: outcome-roadmap
title: Outcome Roadmap
summary: Rebuild a feature roadmap into an outcome roadmap with bets, evidence, and kill criteria.
example: A roadmap of 25 features is relabeled with four outcomes, but the team can staff one bet.
example_out: An outcome roadmap that keeps one staffed bet, parks the rest, and writes a kill criterion.

name: prd-writer
title: PRD Writer
summary: Write a product requirements document with a problem, scope, acceptance signals, and explicit non-goals.
example: A PRD draft lists 15 features and no user outcome.
example_out: A rewritten PRD with one outcome, a small slice, testable acceptance, and the other features as non-goals.

name: pricing-packaging
title: Pricing and Packaging
summary: Frame a pricing and packaging decision as a set of fences and a test, not as a number pulled from a competitor.
example: The company has three tiers that differ only by a feature nobody uses, and discounting is constant.
example_out: A recommendation that treats the discount as the real price and proposes a clearer fence to test.

name: prioritization-rice
title: RICE Prioritization
summary: Prioritize a short list with RICE or a simpler cut, and show the math instead of hiding behind it.
example: A stakeholder wants their idea scored 100 percent confidence so it sorts to the top.
example_out: A note that keeps confidence low, shows the math, and records any strategic override separately.

name: product-analytics-spec
title: Product Analytics Spec
summary: Specify the events and properties a product change needs so the team can tell whether it worked.
example: A spec adds a property for a user's full home address to measure a button click.
example_out: A revised spec that removes the address, defines the click in context, and names the decision it serves.

name: product-brief
title: Product Brief
summary: Write a product brief that frames the problem, the user, and the bet before anyone argues about features.
example: A stakeholder hands over a feature list and asks for a brief by tomorrow.
example_out: A brief that restates the missing problem evidence and refuses to pretend the feature list is a validated bet.

name: roadmap-narrative
title: Roadmap Narrative
summary: Write a roadmap narrative that explains outcomes and sequencing, with dates only where they are real.
example: Sales wants every prospect request placed on next quarter's roadmap.
example_out: A narrative that keeps uncommitted requests in later or off-roadmap, with the reason.

name: stakeholder-prd-review
title: Stakeholder PRD Review
summary: Review a PRD with stakeholders by separating decisions from opinions and parking out-of-scope demands.
example: Sales adds six prospect requests during a PRD review, and engineering thinks they are now committed.
example_out: Notes that park the six requests, restate the surviving scope, and name the decider for any conflict.

name: sunset-plan
title: Sunset Plan
summary: Plan the retirement of a feature or product so users are told the truth and given a path.
example: Engineering wants to delete an API next week that three customers still call.
example_out: A plan that blocks the deletion until notice and a migration owner exist, and flags contract questions.

name: usability-test-plan
title: Usability Test Plan
summary: Plan a usability test that watches someone attempt a task, instead of asking if they like the design.
example: A designer wants to ask ten coworkers whether they like a new color scheme and call it usability.
example_out: A plan with a real task, the right participants, and an explicit note that color preference is not the test.

name: user-story-map
title: User Story Map
summary: Map the user's journey into slices of value so a release is a story, not a pile of tickets.
example: A team has 80 tickets and wants a release that builds the admin console before the user can finish the core job.
example_out: A map whose first slice completes the core job thinly, and parks the admin console.

name: decision-journal
title: Decision Journal
summary: Write a personal decision journal entry with the choice, the expectation, and a review date.
example: A journal entry is edited after a failure to say the risk was always obvious.
example_out: An entry that keeps the original expectation and sets a review without rewriting the past.

name: deep-work-plan
title: Deep Work Plan
summary: Plan focus time around real constraints, with a definition of done for the block.
example: A focus plan depends on coworkers never messaging, with no defer rule.
example_out: A plan with a done statement, a defer rule for mail, and no monitoring of others.

name: email-triage
title: Email Triage
summary: Triage an inbox into reply, schedule, delegate, or drop, without pretending every message is urgent.
example: A triage plan answers newsletters before a customer blocked on a decision.
example_out: A triage that answers the blocked customer first and files the newsletters.

name: meeting-notes
title: Meeting Notes
summary: Write meeting notes that capture decisions, owners, and open questions.
example: Notes say the team agreed though two people dissented.
example_out: Notes that record the dissent and assign owners only to real actions.

name: personal-okr
title: Personal OKRs
summary: Set a few personal objectives that fit the week you actually have.
example: A plan adds a daily two-hour course on top of a 50-hour job with no time removed.
example_out: A smaller set of objectives that fits the real week and names a review.

name: readme-for-a-process
title: Process README
summary: Write a README for a repeated personal or team process so someone else can run it.
example: A README includes a personal access token so others can run a report.
example_out: A README that removes the token, names the secret store, and keeps the real steps.

name: weekly-review
title: Weekly Review
summary: Run a weekly review that closes open loops and picks next week's outcomes.
example: A weekly plan has 40 tasks and 30 hours of existing meetings.
example_out: A review that cuts to a few outcomes and schedules them in the remaining time.

name: writing-brief
title: Writing Brief
summary: Brief a piece of writing so the drafter knows the reader, the point, and the length.
example: A brief says 'write something inspiring about the quarter' with no reader or ask.
example_out: A brief that names the reader, one point, and the action, or stops until those exist.

name: briefing-note
title: Briefing Note
summary: Write a briefing note that states the issue, the options, and the recommendation for a public decision-maker.
example: A brief omits a known cost because it would be unpopular.
example_out: A note that includes the cost and a plain recommendation.

name: consultation-summary
title: Consultation Summary
summary: Summarize a consultation without burying dissenting views.
example: A summary says residents support a plan when most comments opposed it.
example_out: A summary that reports the opposition and refuses the support claim.

name: public-meeting-minutes
title: Public Meeting Minutes
summary: Draft minutes of a public meeting that record motions, votes, and conflicts.
example: Minutes say a motion passed unanimously though a dissent was recorded.
example_out: Minutes that include the dissent and wait for the clerk's approval.

name: records-request-triage
title: Records Request Triage
summary: Triage a records request for scope, search, and exemptions their officer must decide.
example: A manager wants to delete drafts because a request might cover them.
example_out: A triage that forbids deletion and lists locations for the officer to decide.

name: lease-abstract
title: Lease Abstract
summary: Abstract a lease the user provides into dates, money, and notice clauses, without a legal opinion.
example: An abstract assumes a five-year renewal the lease only mentions as a negotiation.
example_out: An abstract that marks renewal as unwritten and lists the counsel question.

name: offer-comparison
title: Offer Comparison
summary: Compare property offers on the terms the user cares about, without advising which legal form to sign.
example: One offer is higher but waives an inspection the seller has not disclosed defects for.
example_out: A matrix that shows the inspection gap and leaves the signature to the principal and their professional.

name: property-due-diligence
title: Property Due Diligence
summary: Build a due-diligence checklist from the deal type and the documents the user can obtain.
example: The checklist is marked complete though no survey was received.
example_out: A checklist that keeps the survey open and refuses a clean conclusion.

name: property-listing-brief
title: Property Listing Brief
summary: Brief a property listing from facts the owner confirmed, with no invented features.
example: A draft says the unit rents for a number the owner has not achieved.
example_out: A brief that removes the invented rent and lists defects the owner already disclosed.

name: rent-roll-review
title: Rent Roll Review
summary: Review a rent roll for inconsistencies, expirations, and concessions the user can see.
example: A roll shows full occupancy while three units are marked 'free rent' with no end date.
example_out: A review that separates free rent from paying occupancy and flags the missing end dates.

name: citation-hygiene
title: Citation Hygiene
summary: Check citations so every claim that needs a source has one the user can verify.
example: A paragraph says 'studies show' and lists no study the user has.
example_out: A revision that replaces the phrase with an assumption or a request for the actual study.

name: claim-limit-note
title: Claim Limit
summary: Limit a sentence to what the study design can support.
example: A sentence says the workshop caused employment. The study asked 20 people at one site how confident they felt.
example_out: A sentence about confidence at that site, with cause and employment removed.

name: consent-script
title: Consent Script
summary: Draft the words a participant hears before they agree, from the study facts the user has.
example: Interviews will be recorded and the script says nobody will know who spoke.
example_out: A script that says the recording exists and names who will hear it.

name: data-availability
title: Data Availability
summary: Write a data-availability statement that matches the files they can actually share.
example: A draft says data are in dba_ripple. No deposit exists. Two files have names and phone numbers.
example_out: A statement that the deposit is not up, and those two files are not in the share set.

name: desk-research
title: Desk Research Brief
summary: Brief desk research so secondary sources are scoped, credited, and not mistaken for primary proof.
example: A landscape scan quotes a vendor's homepage as market share.
example_out: A brief that labels the homepage as a claim, not as market share, and lists the missing independent source.

name: ethics-review-prep
title: Ethics Review Prep
summary: Prepare an ethics review brief for a study involving people, for the review board to judge.
example: A team wants consent language that hides the real purpose from participants.
example_out: A brief that refuses hidden purpose and sends the design to the proper review.

name: evidence-table
title: Evidence Table
summary: Build an evidence table from sources the user supplied, with columns that match the question.
example: A table has effect sizes the user never found in the papers.
example_out: A table with those cells marked unknown and a warning against a numeric conclusion.

name: grant-narrative
title: Grant Narrative
summary: Draft a grant narrative from the funder's questions and the project's real evidence, without inflated impact.
example: A draft claims a partner committed staff, and no letter exists.
example_out: A narrative that moves the partner to 'in discussion' or cuts the claim.

name: interview-guide-research
title: Research Interview Guide
