summary: Write a research interview guide that asks about lived events and records consent the user already requires.
example: A guide starts by asking participants to agree that the product is essential.
example_out: A guide that asks for the last real incident and includes their consent step.

name: literature-review-plan
title: Literature Review Plan
summary: Plan a literature review around a question, with sources the user can actually obtain and no fabricated papers.
example: A draft cites three articles with confident titles the user cannot find.
example_out: A plan that removes unverified citations and sets an inclusion rule before more reading.

name: qualitative-coding
title: Qualitative Coding Plan
summary: Plan qualitative coding so themes come from the data they have, with a second-coder check when it matters.
example: A report lists themes and the user has not provided the supporting lines.
example_out: A coding plan that blocks the report until each theme has a supplied excerpt.

name: replication-check
title: Replication Check
summary: Check whether a result can be rerun from the files the user has.
example: Table 2 cannot be rerun. The analysis script points to a CSV that is not in the folder.
example_out: A note that Table 2 is not rerunnable until that CSV is produced.

name: research-memo
title: Research Memo
summary: Write a research memo that separates evidence, interpretation, and what is still unknown.
example: Five interviews are written up as proof an entire industry is shifting.
example_out: A memo that limits the claim to those five interviews and lists what a larger study would need.

name: research-question
title: Research Question
summary: Sharpen a research question so it is answerable with the methods and access the user has.
example: The question is 'is remote work good' with no population or outcome.
example_out: A narrower question with a population, an outcome, and an explicit non-answer.

name: reviewer-response
title: Reviewer Response
summary: Draft a response to reviewer comments from the changes the authors actually made.
example: Reviewer 2 asked for a second dataset. The authors did not collect one.
example_out: A reply that says the dataset was not collected, with no invented table.

name: source-search-log
title: Search Log
summary: Log the searches and the dates so a review can see what was looked for.
example: A draft methods section lists three databases. The notebook shows two, one of them with zero hits.
example_out: A log of the two searches, including the zero, and the third name removed.

name: survey-instrument
title: Survey Instrument
summary: Draft a survey that measures a defined construct without double-barreled or leading items.
example: An item asks whether the helpful and innovative service was satisfying.
example_out: A draft that splits the ideas, removes the leading praise, and cuts unused demographics.

name: abandoned-cart-recovery
title: Abandoned Cart Recovery
summary: Draft a cart recovery email sequence that reminds without pressuring and states what was in the cart.
example: A sequence says "only 2 left" when the warehouse has 400 units.
example_out: A sequence that removes the false scarcity and earns the second email with a useful reminder.

name: assortment-review
title: Assortment Review
summary: Review an assortment for the customer job, the duplicate, and the item that does not earn its space.
example: A slow-seller list includes an item that was empty for a month.
example_out: A review that separates the stockout from true slow sellers before any drop.

name: loss-prevention-incident
title: Loss Prevention Incident Log
summary: Write a factual loss prevention incident log from the events the user described, without accusations beyond what evidence supports.
example: A log says "the suspect stole the item" based on a single camera angle that does not show concealment.
example_out: A log that says "item not seen at checkout; camera angle does not confirm concealment; LP notified."

name: loyalty-program-design
title: Loyalty Program Design
summary: Draft a loyalty program structure that rewards the behavior the brand actually wants to drive.
example: A program offers 10% back in points but the redemption minimum is higher than the average order, so few members ever cash out.
example_out: A structure that sets a redemption minimum below the average order and discloses the liability cap.

name: marketplace-fee-review
title: Marketplace Fee Review
summary: Review a marketplace fee structure and show the net margin per unit at their price.
example: A review uses last year's referral fee rate and shows a margin that is no longer achievable.
example_out: A review built from the fee schedule they pasted and a note to verify the date.

name: planogram-brief
title: Planogram Brief
summary: Write a shelf placement brief that explains the logic behind the facing sequence and height allocation.
example: A brief gives 8 facings to a slow-selling line because the vendor paid for placement but does not disclose that.
example_out: A brief that uses their sales data and labels any placement that is not data-driven.

name: product-listing-review
title: Product Listing Review
summary: Review an online product listing for accurate claims, complete specs, and images that match what ships.
example: A listing says the item includes a charger but the SKU does not ship one.
example_out: A review that removes the charger claim and flags the image showing one.

name: product-review-response
title: Product Review Response
summary: Draft a response to a customer product review that acknowledges the experience and does not argue.
example: A one-star review says the zipper broke in a week. The response says "we're sorry you feel that way."
example_out: A response that acknowledges the zipper, says what the warranty covers, and invites a direct contact.

name: promotion-review
title: Promotion Review
summary: Review a promotion for margin, inventory, and honest terms.
example: A banner shows a crossed-out price the item never sold for.
example_out: A review that removes the crossed-out price and checks inventory before the banner runs.

name: returns-desk-script
title: Returns Desk Script
summary: Script a returns conversation that follows policy and does not accuse the shopper.
example: A script tells associates to shame the shopper into keeping the item.
example_out: A script that states the policy calmly and escalates exceptions without shame.

name: store-opening-checklist
title: Store Opening Checklist
summary: Write a store opening checklist that confirms safety, cash, and the floor before doors open.
example: A checklist says to prop an alarmed exit so deliveries are easier.
example_out: A checklist that forbids propping the exit and names the person who can delay opening.

name: audit-response
title: Audit Response
summary: Draft a response to an audit request that is complete, tied to evidence, and not misleading.
example: A draft response describes a monthly review that exists only in the policy, not in practice.
example_out: A response that tells the truth about the gap and commits to an owned fix instead of a fictional review.

name: compliance-calendar
title: Compliance Calendar
summary: Build a calendar of obligations the organization already knows it has, with owners and lead time.
example: A team wants every possible global filing listed just in case.
example_out: A calendar of confirmed obligations, with unknowns flagged for counsel instead of invented.

name: conflict-of-interest
title: Conflict of Interest Disclosure
summary: Structure a conflict-of-interest disclosure so a reviewer can see the interest and the decision it touches.
example: An employee wants the disclosure to omit that their sibling owns the bidding vendor.
example_out: A disclosure that includes the sibling relationship and recommends recusal from the award.

name: control-design
title: Control Design
summary: Design a control that prevents or detects a named failure, and specify the evidence it leaves.
example: The control is 'management reviews revenue' with no sample and no sign-off.
example_out: A design that names the sample, the reviewer, and the evidence left behind.

name: ethics-hotline-triage
title: Ethics Hotline Triage
summary: Triage a hotline report toward the right independent handler, without retaliation or a verdict.
example: A report names the division president, and the president asks to handle it personally.
example_out: A triage that routes around the president and refuses retaliation against the reporter.

name: gifts-and-entertainment
title: Gifts and Entertainment
summary: Apply a gifts and entertainment rule to a specific offer, and record the decision.
example: A bidder offers tickets during an open RFP and the draft calls them a friendly dinner.
example_out: A note that names the open RFP, refuses the disguise, and recommends decline or disclosure under their policy.

name: issue-management
title: Issue Management
summary: Record a compliance or control issue with severity, owner, and a dated remediation.
example: An issue is marked closed because the owner said the spreadsheet was updated, with no sample.
example_out: An open issue until a sample shows the control operating, with a dated owner.

name: policy-writer
title: Policy Writer
summary: Draft a policy people can follow, with an owner, an exception path, and a review date.
example: A draft cites several laws from memory to sound serious.
example_out: A draft that removes the invented citations, names an owner, and stays short enough to follow.

name: privacy-impact-assessment
title: Privacy Impact Assessment
summary: Prepare a privacy impact note for a process that collects personal data, for counsel to complete.
example: A new form collects date of birth to personalize a color theme.
example_out: A note that cuts the date of birth and sends any remaining legal question to counsel.

name: records-retention
title: Records Retention Schedule
summary: Draft a retention schedule from the record types they know they keep, with owners and legal questions marked.
triggers: how long do we keep this
example: A team wants a seven-year rule on everything because it sounds safe.
example_out: A draft that refuses the blanket rule, separates business need from legal questions, and protects holds.

name: regulatory-change-log
title: Regulatory Change Log
summary: Log a regulatory change the user has identified, with impact questions and an owner, without giving a legal opinion.
example: A blog post says a rule changed, and the team wants to mark the company compliant today.
example_out: A log entry that sources the blog as unverified, assigns counsel questions, and makes no compliance claim.

name: risk-assessment
title: Risk Assessment
summary: Assess a few real risks with a scenario, a control, and an owner, using the organization's own scale.
example: A workshop list says 'cyber' and 'talent' with no scenario.
example_out: An assessment that rewrites those into specific events or drops them until a scenario exists.

name: sanctions-compliance-process
title: Sanctions Screening Operations
summary: Describe how a legitimate screening process should handle a possible match, for compliance staff. Not evasion advice.
example: Sales wants to tweak a customer name so the screening tool stops flagging it.
example_out: A refusal of the tweak, a pause recommendation, and a handoff to the compliance owner.

name: sox-walkthrough
title: SOX Walkthrough Prep
summary: Prepare a walkthrough of a financial control so the performer can show what they actually do.
example: A manager wants the performer to describe a review that does not happen.
example_out: A prep note that refuses the false story and writes the gap for management.

name: third-party-risk
title: Third-Party Risk
summary: Screen a third party for the risk created by the access and data you will give them.
example: A design tool and a payroll processor are put through an identical unread checklist.
example_out: A note that deepens the payroll review, lightens the design-tool review, and names the owner.

name: activation-gap
title: Activation Gap
summary: Find where new workspaces stall, from the step counts the user exported.
example: 200 trials, 90 created a project, 20 invited a teammate. Activated means the invite.
example_out: A note that the gap is the invite, with no invented reason.

name: churn-save-plan
title: Churn Save Plan
summary: Plan a save offer from the cancel reasons in the export and the offer they can honor.
example: 40 cancels. 22 said a missing export. A draft offers 20 percent off to all of them.
example_out: A plan that does not discount the 22 until the export exists.

name: net-retention-note
title: Net Retention Note
summary: Compute net retention only from the starting and ending revenue they provide for the same accounts.
example: A slide says 120 percent NRR. The file has one revenue pool and no same-account cohort.
example_out: A note that refuses the 120 percent until the same accounts are identified.

name: plan-limit-note
title: Plan Limit Note
summary: Write the limit a plan enforces, and the message the user sees when they hit it.
example: The product blocks at 5,000 rows. The message still says they can export everything.
example_out: A message that names 5,000 and the block.

name: pricing-page-note
title: Pricing Page Note
summary: Check a pricing page against the plans and the limits they actually enforce.
example: The page says unlimited exports. The product stops at 5,000 rows.
example_out: A note to change the page to 5,000 rows.

name: saas-weekly-metrics
title: SaaS Weekly Metrics
summary: Read a weekly SaaS export and say what moved, without a benchmark from memory.
example: The export has MRR and churn. Activation is blank. A slide adds a 120 percent NRR from memory.
example_out: A note with the export figures and a blank activation and NRR.

name: security-answer-sheet
title: Security Answer Sheet
summary: Answer a security questionnaire from documents the company has, and leave the rest blank.
example: A question asks for the SOC 2 report. The folder has no report. A draft says yes, in progress.
example_out: An answer of not in the file, with no in-progress claim they did not document.

name: trial-to-paid
title: Trial To Paid
summary: Report trial-to-paid from the cohort dates in the export.
example: September trials are still inside a 14-day trial. August finished at 18 of 100.
example_out: A note that reports August and leaves September open.

name: account-plan
title: Account Plan
summary: Write an account plan for a named customer that focuses on their goals, the whitespace you can evidence, and the next plays.
example: An account manager owns a renewal and wants a strategic plan, but the only known goal is 'get through this year's audit'.
example_out: A plan anchored on the audit goal, with one evidenced expansion idea and the rest marked unknown.

name: champion-map
title: Champion Map
summary: Test whether a supposed champion can actually move a deal, and plan how to support them ethically.
example: The day-to-day user replies quickly but has never met procurement, and the seller calls them the champion.
example_out: A map that relabels the user as a coach and names the missing introduction to the economic buyer.

name: competitive-battlecard
title: Competitive Battlecard
summary: Build a battlecard from proof and trap questions, without invented competitor weaknesses.
example: Reps claim a rival 'is going out of business' with no source.
example_out: A card that deletes the rumor, states a sourced product difference, and names the segment where the rival is a better fit.

name: deal-desk-review
title: Deal Desk Review
summary: Review a nonstandard deal for margin, precedent, and delivery risk before anyone signs.
example: Sales wants a custom integration included free to win a logo, and delivery has not estimated it.
example_out: A note that conditions any approval on a delivery estimate and names the precedent risk of free custom work.

name: demo-storyboard
title: Demo Storyboard
summary: Storyboard a demo around the buyer's job, with proof points and a stop time, not a feature tour.
example: A 45-minute demo deck has 30 features, and the buyer only asked how exceptions get resolved.
example_out: A storyboard with one exception-resolution scene, two supporting proofs, and the other features parked.

name: discovery-call
title: Discovery Call
summary: Plan and review a discovery call that uncovers the buyer's problem, timing, and authority without pitching over them.
triggers: what should I ask the buyer
example: A salesperson has 30 minutes with an operations lead and usually spends 25 of them on slides.
example_out: A call plan with six questions, a definition of a qualified next step, and a note template that separates facts from guesses.

name: expansion-play
title: Expansion Play
summary: Design an expansion conversation that starts from a realized outcome, not from the seller's quota gap.
example: A rep wants to cross-sell a second module, but the first module has no confirmed outcome.
example_out: A play that pauses expansion and defines the adoption proof required before a second offer is made.

name: forecast-call
title: Forecast Call
summary: Produce a sales forecast from evidence categories, not from a sum of hope.
example: Leadership wants a number that is 30 percent above the deals with a real buyer process.
example_out: A forecast range, a clear gap to the hoped-for number, and two inspections, with no fake deals added to close the gap.

name: mutual-action-plan
title: Mutual Action Plan
summary: Draft a mutual action plan that shows the buyer's steps and the seller's steps on one timeline.
example: A seller wants a mutual action plan, but the buyer has not named a security reviewer.
example_out: A plan that leaves security review unowned and refuses to print a close date as agreed.

name: objection-handling
title: Objection Handling
summary: Answer a sales objection with evidence and a question, not with pressure or made-up proof.
example: A buyer says 'you are too expensive' before any outcome has been quantified.
example_out: A response that treats the comment as unquantified, asks what it is being compared with, and does not invent a discount or a logo.

name: pipeline-review
title: Pipeline Review
summary: Review a pipeline so stages mean evidence, and stuck deals get a next action or an exit.
example: A pipeline has 30 opportunities and 18 have no dated next step.
example_out: A review that rewinds or removes undated deals and names one coaching point about buyer-owned next steps.

name: pricing-negotiation
title: Pricing Negotiation
summary: Prepare a negotiation around price and tradeoffs, with a walk-away and no deceptive concessions.
example: Procurement asked for 20 percent off, and the seller's floor is 8 percent with a two-year term available as a trade.
example_out: A give-get plan that offers the term trade, holds the floor, and includes a walk-away line with no fake competitor.

name: proposal-writer
title: Proposal Writer
summary: Write a proposal that restates the buyer's problem, the offer, the proof, and the ask, without invented ROI.
example: A seller wants a proposal for a buyer who has not confirmed the problem or the budget.
example_out: A short proposal skeleton that refuses invented ROI and lists the two facts still required before price is presented as final.

name: qualification-meddic
title: MEDDIC Qualification
summary: Qualify an opportunity with MEDDIC-style evidence so the forecast is not a mood.
example: A deal is forecast for this month, and the only contact is a manager who likes the product but cannot sign.
example_out: A brief that marks economic buyer and process as missing and refuses to call the deal committed.

name: renewal-save
title: Renewal Save
summary: Plan a renewal that is at risk by finding the real grievance and offering a remedy inside policy.
example: A customer will not renew because nobody completed onboarding, and the rep wants to offer 30 percent off.
example_out: A save plan that leads with an onboarding remedy and holds the discount until a commercial problem is actually shown.

name: rfp-response
title: RFP Response
summary: Decide whether to answer an RFP and, if yes, draft a response that is compliant, true, and selective.
example: An RFP asks for a certification the company has not achieved and sales wants to answer 'yes, in progress' in the yes box.
example_out: A plan that answers no or exception, explains the in-progress status outside the yes box, and flags a no-bid choice if the item is mandatory.

name: sales-email-sequence
title: Sales Email Sequence
summary: Write a short, truthful outreach or follow-up sequence that earns a reply without deception.
example: A rep wants a five-email sequence that pretends the buyer asked for information.
example_out: A three-note sequence with a real observation, one ask, and no fake inquiry, plus a stop after the third note.

name: sales-playbook
title: Sales Playbook
summary: Write one sales play for a repeated situation, with talk track, proof, and exit criteria.
example: Reps keep promising a feature that is not shipped when they hear a competitor's name.
example_out: A competitive play with a question track, a ban on unshipped features, and an exit criterion based on buyer criteria.

name: territory-plan
title: Territory Plan
summary: Plan a territory from the accounts that fit, the capacity of the seller, and a weekly rhythm.
example: A rep has 200 accounts and ten hours a week for prospecting after live deals.
example_out: A tiered plan that fully works a small set, parks the rest, and fits the ten hours.

name: win-loss-review
title: Win Loss Review
summary: Review wins and losses to find a pattern the team can change, not a story that flatters the winner.
example: The team lost three deals and wants to discount, but buyer notes mention slow security review.
example_out: A review that treats security-review speed as the pattern to test and does not approve a discount from this evidence alone.

name: access-review
title: Access Review
summary: Review who has access to a sensitive system and remove access that no longer has a reason.
example: A shared admin login is still used after three people left the company.
example_out: A review that recommends unique accounts, lists the leavers for removal, and does not request the shared password.

name: backup-and-restore-test
title: Backup and Restore Test
summary: Plan a restore test that proves a backup can be recovered, not merely that a backup job ran.
example: The team says backups are fine because the nightly job is green, and nobody has restored one.
example_out: A restore test into a non-production target, with a recorded time and a ban on production overwrite.

name: identity-hardening
title: Identity Hardening
summary: Plan identity hardening around administrators, joiners and leavers, and phishing-resistant sign-in where they can support it.
example: Contractors keep admin access for months after the contract ends.
example_out: A plan that ties leaver dates to access removal and refuses any request for live codes.

name: incident-response-coord
title: Incident Response Coordination
summary: Coordinate a security incident response with roles, containment, and communications that do not speculate.
example: A chat is about to tell customers data was stolen before anyone has confirmed access.
example_out: A coordination note that holds the claim, assigns a lead, and forbids log destruction.

name: logging-and-detection
title: Logging and Detection
summary: Specify defensive logs and alerts for a likely abuse, without writing an intrusion guide.
example: A team wants an alert on data export but also asks to log every keystroke of a department.
example_out: A detection note for the export event that refuses the keystroke surveillance.

name: privacy-by-design
title: Privacy by Design
summary: Review a feature for data minimization, purpose, and user-facing honesty before it ships.
example: A feature stores a full ID document to personalize a greeting.
example_out: A note that cuts the document, keeps the display name if needed, and flags the notice gap.

name: sbom-and-supply-chain
title: Software Supply Chain Note
summary: Review a software supply chain concern using the inventory the user has, without pretending a scan you did not run.
example: A release is built on a laptop and nobody can list the dependencies.
example_out: A note that makes inventory and a repeatable build the first actions, with no invented component list.

name: secrets-handling
title: Secrets Handling
summary: Review how a secret is stored and rotated, and remove it from code, tickets, and chat.
example: A key was committed and the user pastes it into chat asking if it looks real.
example_out: A response that refuses to repeat the key, tells them to rotate it, and describes a store reference.

name: secure-code-review
title: Secure Code Review
summary: Review a change for defensive security issues and request fixes, without writing an exploit.
example: A pull request logs a session token while debugging a login bug.
example_out: A blocking review that requires the log removed, the token rotated, and no token reprinted in the comment.

name: security-awareness-brief
title: Security Awareness Brief
summary: Draft a short awareness brief for a real behavior, without fear theater or trick phishing against employees.
example: A manager wants to embarrass an employee who clicked a bad link by naming them in an all-hands.
example_out: A brief that teaches reporting, omits the name, and refuses public shaming.

name: security-exception
title: Security Exception
summary: Record a security exception with an owner, an expiry, and a compensating control.
example: A team wants to skip MFA forever because a vendor integration is inconvenient.
example_out: A time-boxed exception only if a compensating control exists, otherwise a refusal of the permanent waiver.

name: security-policy-draft
title: Security Policy Draft
summary: Draft a short security policy for one topic, in language employees can follow, marked for the security owner.
example: The company wants a password policy and currently shares a team login.
example_out: A draft that bans shared logins, sets an owner, and leaves legal penalties to counsel.

name: security-requirements
title: Security Requirements
summary: Write defensive security requirements for a feature so engineering can build controls without exploit instructions.
example: A new export feature has no statement about who may export customer data.
example_out: Requirements for authorization, audit, and a safe allow-and-deny test, with no attack procedure.

name: tabletop-exercise
title: Tabletop Exercise
summary: Plan a tabletop exercise that practices decisions under a security scenario without live attacks.
example: The team wants a 'realistic' exercise that sends malware to employees.
example_out: A paper inject plan that practices notification decisions and refuses malware.

name: vendor-security-review
title: Vendor Security Review
summary: Review a vendor's security claims against the data you will share, without granting a fake certification.
example: A team wants to send customer files to a tool because its website says 'enterprise grade'.
example_out: A review that lists unanswered questions and refuses to treat the slogan as a control.

name: vulnerability-triage
title: Vulnerability Triage
summary: Triage a reported vulnerability for severity, owner, and a patch path. Do not develop the vulnerability.
example: A bot reports a critical issue in a library the team is not sure they use.
example_out: A triage that first confirms presence, refuses an exploit, and sets an owner for the confirmation.

name: content-refresh-seo
title: Search Refresh
summary: Decide whether an old URL should be updated, from the query and the stale claim.
example: The permit page ranks for a query they still want, and the fee is wrong.
example_out: A refresh of the same URL, with the new fee and the date, not a second URL.

name: index-coverage
title: Index Coverage
summary: Read an index export and say which URLs are out and why the export says so.
example: 30 blog URLs are excluded by a noindex left on from a March test.
example_out: A note to remove that noindex, with no ranking promise.

name: internal-links
title: Internal Link Plan
summary: Plan internal links from pages that exist to pages that answer the next question.
example: The furnace page should point to the oil-change page with the anchor 'emergency plumber'.
example_out: A plan that rejects that anchor and uses words that match the oil-change page.

name: keyword-map
title: Keyword Map
summary: Map queries to pages the user already has, using only queries they exported or listed.
example: Harbor Goods has a furnace page and an oil-change page. They listed eight queries. Two match no page.
example_out: A map of the six matches and a gap list of two, with no new doorway URLs.

name: local-seo-note
title: Local SEO Note
summary: Check a local listing and a location page against the name, address, and phone the user uses.
example: The listing says open Sunday. The shop is closed Sunday. The phone matches.
example_out: A note to change Sunday hours and to leave the phone alone.

name: search-intent
title: Search Intent
summary: Say what the searcher is trying to do, from the query and the page the user has.
example: The query is 'furnace repair Airdrie'. The page is a brand story with no service area and no phone.
example_out: A note that the page does not answer the query until the service facts are on it.

name: serp-gap
title: SERP Gap
summary: Compare the user's page to what they can see on the results page, without inventing ranks.
example: They looked at the query and their page has no city and no hours. They did not record a rank.
example_out: A gap note about city and hours, with no rank claim.

name: technical-seo-note
title: Technical SEO Note
summary: Turn crawl findings the user exported into a fix list a developer can accept or reject.
example: A crawl of 40 URLs shows 12 furnace pages missing a title and the blog blocked by a test noindex.
example_out: A fix list for the title template and a note to remove the test noindex, with no traffic promise.

name: books-handoff
title: Books Handoff
summary: Hand a bookkeeper the accounts, the open items, and the access that is not a shared password.
example: August does not tie on the till. Two supplier bills are missing. She offered her bank password.
example_out: A handoff that lists the two bills and refuses the shared password.

name: busy-season-plan
title: Busy Season Plan
summary: Plan the busy weeks from last year's pattern and this year's staff.
example: Last December Saturdays did 40 cars. She has two techs this year, not four.
example_out: A plan sized to two techs, not to last year's 40.

name: first-employee-note
title: First Employee Note
summary: List what an owner must decide before a first hire, without inventing employment law.
example: Diane wants a Saturday helper at $18 an hour. She has not checked payroll or insurance.
example_out: A note that lists the open checks and does not say the hire is legal.

name: local-service-offer
title: Local Service Offer
summary: Write a local offer from the price and the hours the owner can honor.
example: An ad says half-price oil changes all month. She can do six a day and only priced Friday.
example_out: An offer for Friday, six cars, at the price she set.

name: local-supplier-pick
title: Local Supplier Pick
summary: Pick between quotes the owner has, on price, lead time, and the terms on the page.
example: Two oil quotes. One is cheaper and has no return term. The other is local and takes returns.
example_out: A pick that shows both and does not hide the missing return term.

name: owner-cash-huddle
title: Owner Cash Huddle
summary: Set the week's cash picture from the till, the bills due, and the owner's buffer.
example: The till has $4,200. Rent of $3,000 is Thursday. A customer might pay $2,000.
example_out: A huddle that does not spend the $2,000 and shows Thursday against the buffer.

name: owner-draw-note
title: Owner Draw Note
summary: Separate an owner draw from wages and from money the business still owes.
example: She wants $2,000 out. Rent is unpaid. The bookkeeper calls these draws, not wages.
example_out: A note that holds the draw until rent is paid.

name: permit-checklist-local
title: Local Permit Checklist
summary: List the permits the owner already knows they need, and the ones they have not checked.
example: She has a business licence and a fee sheet for a sidewalk display at $75. She has not asked about a sign.
example_out: A list that includes the licence and the $75 sheet, and leaves the sign unchecked.

name: annual-planning-cycle
title: Annual Planning Cycle
summary: Design a planning calendar that connects strategy, money, and team capacity without a three-month planning fog.
example: A COO wants next year's planning to finish before December instead of drifting into February.
example_out: A backward calendar from the approval date, two draft rounds, required inputs, and an explicit capacity check.

name: board-meeting-facilitator
title: Board Meeting Facilitator
summary: Design a board agenda that spends time on decisions and exceptions, and produce a clean minute skeleton afterward.
example: A chair has 90 minutes and three decisions: a budget revision, a key hire, and a customer concentration risk.
example_out: A timed agenda with decisions first, plus a minute skeleton that records the ask, the vote line, and actions.

name: board-memo-writer
title: Board Memo Writer
summary: Draft a board memo that leads with the decision, the ask, and the risk, not a recap of activity.
example: The CEO needs a pre-read asking the board to approve a hiring pause until a renewal lands.
example_out: A two-page memo with the ask, the cash implication, two alternatives, and the decision requested at the meeting.

name: change-leadership
title: Change Leadership
summary: Plan how a specific change will be adopted, including who loses something and how you will support them.
example: Finance is moving the company from monthly spreadsheets to a shared close calendar and managers are ignoring it.
example_out: An adoption plan that names Tuesday behaviors, manager support, the loss of local flexibility, and one observable adoption metric.

name: competitive-strategy
title: Competitive Strategy
summary: Explain how you win against a named alternative, including the status quo, without inventing competitor secrets.
example: A team keeps losing to spreadsheets, not to the named software rival, and wants a strategy note.
example_out: A note that treats the spreadsheet as the main alternative, names the buyer you will not chase, and lists the proof still missing.

name: corporate-narrative
title: Corporate Narrative
summary: Write the company story employees and customers can repeat without sliding into hype.
example: A team has five conflicting About pages and wants one narrative before a launch.
example_out: A sentence, a paragraph, and a half page that share one customer change and only the proof the user provided.

name: culture-diagnostic
title: Culture Diagnostic
summary: Describe how the culture actually behaves, using evidence, and name one habit worth changing.
example: A founder says the culture is 'like a family' but missed commitments have no consequence.
example_out: A diagnostic that uses the user's incidents, names the accountability gap, and proposes one ritual rather than a new values poster.

name: decision-log
title: Decision Log
summary: Record an important decision so a later reader can see the choice, the alternatives, and what would reopen it.
example: A leadership team chose to pause a second product line after a renewal slipped, and they want the reason written down.
example_out: A one-page decision record with the choice, the alternative, the cash fact that drove it, and the condition that would reopen it.

name: executive-offsite-design
title: Executive Offsite Design
summary: Design an offsite that leaves with decisions, not a pile of flip charts.
example: A CEO has one day with the exec team and wants to leave with a focus decision and a hiring principle.
example_out: An agenda with two outcomes, pre-reads, a decision block for each, and a closing owner assignment.

name: executive-one-pager
title: Executive One-Pager
summary: Compress a complex issue into a single page a busy executive can act on.
example: A general manager needs the CEO to approve a price test and currently has a 14-page appendix.
example_out: A one-page brief with the test, the risk, three facts, and a yes-or-no ask.

name: founder-decision-review
title: Founder Decision Review
summary: Help a founder pressure-test a lonely decision before they announce it.
triggers: am I about to make a mistake
example: A solo founder wants to fire their first salesperson before a board meeting in two days and is unsure.
example_out: A review that restates the decision, separates facts from fear, names reversibility, and leaves the call with the founder.

name: go-to-market-brief
title: Go-to-Market Brief
summary: Brief a launch or a new motion so sales, product, and marketing are aiming at the same buyer and offer.
triggers: how do we take this to market
example: A product is ready for a design-partner release and the teams disagree on who the buyer is.
example_out: A brief with one buyer, one staffed channel, enablement limits, and a 60-day kill metric.

name: ma-screening
title: M&A Screening
summary: Screen an acquisition or partnership idea before anyone spends serious diligence money.
example: A CEO received a teaser for a small competitor and wants to know if it is even worth a conversation.
example_out: A screening memo with the strategic gap, buy-versus-build, five must-be-true tests, and a single next question before advisors are hired.

name: market-entry-assessment
title: Market Entry Assessment
summary: Test whether a new segment or geography deserves a real bet, using the user's evidence rather than a borrowed market-size slide.
example: A domestic software company asks whether to open a UK motion next quarter because two inbound leads arrived.
example_out: An assessment that defines the segment, prices a 90-day test, names the compliance questions for counsel, and does not treat two leads as a market.

name: north-star-metric
title: North Star Metric
summary: Choose one north-star metric that reflects customer value, plus a handful of input metrics the team can move.
example: A marketplace is debating GMV versus successful jobs completed as the company metric.
example_out: A definition of the chosen metric, why the alternative loses, three input metrics, and a counter-metric that protects quality.

name: okrs-and-scorecard
title: OKRs and Scorecard
summary: Write objectives and key results that measure outcomes, then pair them with a weekly operating scorecard.
example: A product lead wants Q3 OKRs and offers 'ship mobile app' and 'improve NPS' with no baseline.
example_out: Two outcome objectives, key results with baselines and sources, and a weekly scorecard of five numbers tied to those results.

name: operating-cadence
title: Operating Cadence
summary: Design the weekly, monthly, and quarterly meetings that keep a strategy alive without drowning the team.
example: A 40-person company has eleven recurring leadership meetings and still misses hiring and cash decisions.
example_out: A three-loop cadence, the meetings to cancel, the pre-read owner for each loop, and a six-week pilot test.

name: portfolio-prioritization
title: Portfolio Prioritization
summary: Rank a set of initiatives by constraint, not by who argued last, and make the cut visible.
example: A leadership team has 22 active initiatives and 9 managers, and wants a portfolio cut before annual planning.
example_out: A continue, pause, and stop list tied to manager capacity, with the reason each stopped item is waiting.

name: scenario-planning
title: Scenario Planning
summary: Build a small set of contrasting futures and the early signs that tell you which one you are in.
example: A services firm wants to know how to plan hiring if a key public-sector contract is delayed by two quarters.
example_out: Three named scenarios, the signposts for each, and a hiring move tied to the delay signpost rather than to hope.

name: stakeholder-map
title: Stakeholder Map
summary: Map who can help or block a decision, and how to engage them without manipulation.
example: A plant manager wants to change the shift pattern and knows the union rep and two supervisors are uneasy.
example_out: A map of actors, their stated concerns, and a plain engagement sequence that does not hide the effect on hours.

name: strategic-plan-builder
title: Strategic Plan Builder
summary: Turn a vague ambition into a one-page strategy with a real choice, a few bets, and what you will not do.
example: A founder says the company should 'become the platform for mid-market clinics' but the team is still closing the first ten customers by hand.
example_out: A one-page plan that chooses a beachhead, names three bets, lists what will wait, and sets a 90-day review with kill criteria.

name: war-room-brief
title: War Room Brief
summary: Stand up a short-lived response when a serious business issue needs daily focus, without turning panic into a permanent process.
example: A key supplier missed a shipment and three major customers will stock out within a week.
example_out: A 48-hour brief with an owner, the decisions required today, a truthful customer message draft, and an end condition.

name: customs-packet-check
title: Customs Packet Check
summary: Check a shipment packet for the documents the user says the lane requires.
example: A Calgary-to-US packet is missing the commercial invoice. Someone suggested describing the filters as samples.
example_out: A check that holds the packet and rejects the samples description.

name: demand-plan-review
title: Demand Plan Review
summary: Review a demand plan for bias, assumptions, and the one driver that would change supply.
example: The plan repeats last year's hockey stick and actuals have missed it three times.
example_out: A review that flags the bias and refuses to treat the hockey stick as the base.

name: dock-exception-note
title: Dock Exception
summary: Record a dock exception with the count, the PO, and the photo or tally they have.
example: PO 5521 said 40 filters. The tally is 32. The seal note says intact.
example_out: A note for 8 short, stock available 32, no theft claim.

name: inventory-policy
title: Inventory Policy
summary: Set an inventory policy from service target, lead time, and demand variability they can show.
example: A buyer wants six weeks of safety stock because it feels safe, with a two-week lead time.
example_out: A note that asks for the service target and variability before accepting six weeks.

name: landed-cost
title: Landed Cost Review
summary: Build a landed-cost view from cost elements the user can support, so a buy decision sees the full cash cost.
example: A cheaper invoice price is recommended, and nobody added international freight.
example_out: A note that holds the recommendation until freight is included or explicitly unknown.

name: lead-time-review
title: Lead Time Review
summary: Compare the lead time in the system to the receipts the user can show.
example: The system says 14 days. Three receipts took 26, 28, and 27 days.
example_out: A note to change the system only after those three receipts are accepted as the pattern.

name: logistics-exception
title: Logistics Exception
summary: Handle a logistics exception with the customer impact, the options, and a truthful status.
example: A carrier missed a pickup and the draft tells the customer the order is on time.
example_out: A note that states the miss, lists real options, and removes the on-time claim.

name: otif-review
title: OTIF Review
summary: Review on-time-in-full from the shipments the user counted, split by cause.
example: 94 shipments, 86 on time in full, target 95. 6 of the misses followed a same-week forecast change.
example_out: A review that reports 86 percent and separates those 6.

name: purchase-order-control
title: Purchase Order Control
summary: Review purchase-order control so orders are approved, received, and matched without informal side deals.
example: A team lead emails a supplier directly to avoid the PO system.
example_out: A review that treats the email order as a control break and names the missing approval.

name: returns-process
title: Returns Process
summary: Design a returns process with a reason code, a disposition, and a customer promise you can keep.
example: The website promises instant refunds and the warehouse has not inspected the unit.
example_out: A process that aligns the promise with inspection and keeps inventory records honest.

name: s-and-op
title: Sales and Operations Planning
summary: Brief an S&OP cycle so demand, supply, and a decision meet in one forum.
example: Sales brings a new forecast to the meeting that supply has not seen.
example_out: A brief that stops the decision until both sides use the same number, then records the gap.

name: safety-stock
title: Safety Stock Review
summary: Review safety stock for a few items so cash is not trapped in a habit.
example: Every item is set to 90 days because the spreadsheet default says so.
example_out: A review that pilots a reduction on items with no risk story and leaves named risks alone.

name: shortage-playbook
title: Shortage Playbook
summary: Allocate a shortage fairly against a stated rule, and communicate it without favoritism hidden in a spreadsheet.
example: A planner gives the scarce item to the loudest salesperson's account.
example_out: A playbook that applies a written rule, records exceptions, and tells affected customers the truth.

name: sku-cut-review
title: SKU Cut Review
summary: Propose SKUs to stop reordering from the movement and the stock the user shows.
example: Four SKUs sold zero in 90 days. One is a winter blade they must keep. Stock is still on the shelf.
example_out: A stop-reorder list of three, with the winter blade held.

name: supplier-onboarding
title: Supplier Onboarding
summary: Onboard a supplier with the documents, access, and first-order check the company actually requires.
example: A supplier emails new bank details from a free mail account and wants the next payment sent there.
example_out: A checklist that blocks the change until their verified channel confirms it.

name: supplier-risk-note
title: Supplier Risk Note
summary: Note a supplier risk from the evidence the buyer has, without a mood score.
example: SKU 1044 has one supplier and a 28-day lead time. Last month they missed 14 units.
example_out: A note that names the single source and the 14-unit miss, with no invented score.

name: supplier-scorecard
title: Supplier Scorecard
summary: Score a supplier on the outcomes in the agreement, using evidence rather than the last meeting's mood.
example: A supplier is blamed for shortages after the forecast doubled with no notice.
example_out: A scorecard that records the forecast change as a buyer cause and limits the supplier miss to evidenced gaps.

name: emissions-inventory-brief
title: Emissions Inventory Brief
summary: Brief an emissions inventory from activity data they have, with factors labeled and gaps visible.
example: A report states net zero because one office bought offsets, and no inventory exists.
example_out: A brief that refuses the claim and lists the missing activity data.

name: esg-disclosure-outline
title: ESG Disclosure Outline
summary: Outline an ESG disclosure around metrics the company can evidence this year.
example: A report outline claims alignment with a standard nobody has mapped.
example_out: An outline that labels alignment as not yet assessed and lists only sourced metrics.

name: supplier-sustainability-questionnaire
title: Supplier Sustainability Questionnaire
summary: Review supplier sustainability answers for evidence, not for a score that hides missing proof.
example: A supplier says it is certified and attaches no certificate.
example_out: A review that marks the certification unverified and asks for the document.

name: sustainability-claim-review
title: Sustainability Claim Review
summary: Review a sustainability claim for substantiation before it is published.
example: Packaging says 'carbon neutral' and the only support is an intention.
example_out: A review that removes the phrase until the basis exists.

name: delivery-exception
title: Delivery Exception
summary: Handle a failed delivery with a new promise you can keep and a reason the customer can understand.
example: A text says the parcel was delivered though the driver marked an access failure.
example_out: An exception plan that corrects the status and offers a real redelivery window.

name: dispatch-plan
title: Dispatch Plan
summary: Plan a dispatch from orders, hours, and equipment limits the user stated.
example: A dispatcher is told to log a break that did not happen so the route stays legal on paper.
example_out: A plan that refuses the false log and shows which order must move instead.

name: fleet-safety-review
title: Fleet Safety Review
summary: Review a fleet safety pattern from incidents they logged, and pick one control.
example: A review suggests not reporting a minor crash so the score stays clean.
example_out: A review that refuses the non-report and assigns a control for the actual pattern.
